articles.title: Ukraine says deadly new strikes dash peace hopes
articles.excerpt: Ukraine on Monday said that Russian strikes on a school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people, dashing fragile…
articles.fullText:
Ukraine on Monday said that Russian strikes on a school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people, dashing fragile hopes of "progress toward peace" after a local ceasefire in the south expired without violations.

Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours, Kyiv said.

A rare pause in the fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump to enable a mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ended on Sunday after starting on Tuesday, with neither side reporting breaches.

But hours after the truce, Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia, adjacent to Kherson, with repeated strikes that killed at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said.

Some of the dead had come to collect aid at a local school.

Footage posted by the Ukrainian emergency services showed the building reduced to piles of smouldering rubble and rescuers working at the site.

"Every Monday, humanitarian aid was distributed to people there," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his daily address.

"The Russians carried out the first strike just as people arrived — several aerial bombs. Then, there was a repeat strike — more aerial bombs, this time targeting the shelter."

Among those killed were "two rescue workers and four police officers", acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram.

The service named the rescuers as two 44-year-olds: Denys Konovalenko and Oleksy Sushchevsky.

"Every day, they went out to help people, working in dangerous conditions and risking their own lives to save others," it said in a statement.

Zelensky said that after the Oleshky truce, "There was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible.

"With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings. There must be a response to this."

The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours, which is grinding through its fifth year after killing hundreds of thousands of people and displacing millions.

A senior Ukrainian figure told AFP on Sunday that Russia refused a Ukrainian offer to extend the truce.

Kyiv's military also alleged that Moscow had used the pause in fighting to "fortify its positions".

The Kremlin did not deny the accusations, with its spokesman Dmitry Peskov telling reporters on Monday: "This is a completely normal practice in such situations."

He alleged the Ukrainian army had also used pauses in fighting in the past to regroup.

Moscow saw the Oleshky humanitarian mission as "successful", Peskov added, praising the "good cooperation between all sides" and singling out the role of its human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova.

Lantratova oversaw the ceasefire alongside her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets in one of the most substantial instances of Russian-Ukrainian cooperation since the start of the war.

The mission saw people evacuated to both Ukraine-controlled territory and Moscow-annexed Crimea.

The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned "at the moment".

US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume next week, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.

US President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but there has been no breakthrough.

The talks — to be held November 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff said — come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.

Both Russia and Ukraine said overnight that their emergency warnings apps were hacked in apparent cyberattacks that came hours after the truce had ended.

Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after false alerts of a radiation threat were sent to millions.

The warning system provides vital information about incoming Russian drones and missiles.

Russia has intensified its attacks this year, firing ballistic missiles and fast jet-powered drones, both of which are hard to intercept.

Moscow said that an app belonging to its emergency situations ministry that also warns of attacks had been hacked, too.

The app is not widely used in Russia, where warnings of Ukrainian drone attacks are not as common and typically sent by text message in border regions. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Oil prices plunge on US-Iran hopes, stocks end mixed
articles.excerpt: Oil prices tumbled more than seven percent on Monday, the eve of crucial midterm elections in the United States, as…
articles.fullText:
Oil prices tumbled more than seven percent on Monday, the eve of crucial midterm elections in the United States, as signals that Tehran and Washington were renewing dialogue boosted hopes of ending the Middle East war.

Iran on Monday said "intensive" exchanges were underway with Washington and offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, as efforts escalated to avert a return to conflict.

Earlier, the Axios news outlet reported that US Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks.

That was the highest-level move from US President Donald Trump's administration in months.

Again Capital's John Kilduff described investors as experiencing "a violent change in market sentiment," adding that "we went from really, I think, expecting a major offensive after tomorrow's US elections to a potential breakthrough," he said.

"All these losses will be taken right back if this doesn't pan out," Kilduff said.

The steep drop in oil prices translated into weakness among petroleum stocks.

But Wall Street shares otherwise began the day with promise, bouncing back after last Friday's rout precipitated by worries over the tech industry's massive artificial intelligence spending.

But tech shares came under pressure as the session progressed, with the tech-focused Nasdaq slumping 1.1 percent.

"This is still a market that is on edge," said Joseph Zidle, chief market strategist at Cresset Capital, who described unease about midterm elections as adding to worries about the AI boom.

"The two of them are actually related," Zidle said of midterms and AI, noting that opposition to data centres has animated many campaigns.

AI has been "on the ballot in so many places, both blue and red," Zidle said.

"It seems like data centres are part of the kitchen table issues."

Pollsters expect Democrats to win back control of the House of Representatives, but view Trump's Republican Party as potentially able to maintain a majority in the Senate.

The loss of total Republican dominance would push the president into unfamiliar and uncomfortable territory: a lame duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.

"Investors are bracing for a fresh round of turbulence ahead of US midterm election fireworks while they assess the extent that companies are burning through cash to keep the AI bonfires burning," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

Earnings this week will come from Apple, which reports after the close of trading on Monday, as well as Advanced Micro Devices and software titan Palantir will be closely watched this week.

Shares in Apple fell 1.8 percent.

The S&P 500 fell 0.5 percent, to 7,541, the Dow rose 0.4 percent, to 51,984, while the Nasdaq fell 1.1 percent, to 25,164. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Man arrested over suspected spiked drink

Police have arrested a 61-year-old man suspected of adding an unknown substance to a 33-year-old woman's drink at a bar in Tsim Sha Tsui.

Police received a report just before 5am on Sunday that a woman had fallen ill after drinking a beverage at a bar on Mody Road, with suspicions that the drink had been spiked.

She was conscious and taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital for treatment.

The Yau Tsim Criminal Investigation Support Team took up the case and made the arrest in Central on Monday.

The man is being held for further questioning on suspicion of administering poison with intent to harm.

Japanese former adult film star turned DJ, Mao Hamasaki, has said she fell ill after having a drink that she said had been tampered with during a Halloween event.

A 54-year-old woman died early on Tuesday after reportedly being knocked down by a private car in Tuen Mun, with the driver arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving causing death.

The accident happened at about 11.09pm on Monday along Castle Peak Road in Hung Shui Kiu, as the car was travelling towards Yuen Long.

The woman suffered serious head injuries and was rushed to Tuen Mun Hospital in an unconscious state, where she was certified dead at 0.17am on Tuesday.

The 53-year-old male driver was arrested and is being detained for further enquiries.

The case is being investigated by the Special Investigation Team of Traffic, New Territories North.

articles.title: Everton edge Newcastle to go seventh in Premier League
articles.excerpt: Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James'…
articles.fullText:
Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James' Park on Monday.

Barry netted early in the second half to lift Everton into seventh place in the Premier League and leave Newcastle in 13th.

Newcastle midfielder Jacob Ramsey was sent off in the final seconds for a crude foul on Harrison Armstrong.

It was a fitting end to another painful defeat for Saudi-funded Newcastle, who have lost four of their past five matches in all competitions, winning just twice in their past seven.

Jaissle and his players were booed off at half-time and again after the final whistle as the German coach begins to feel the heat in his first season in charge.

Hired following Eddie Howe's surprise close-season exit, former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli boss Jaissle has struggled to make an impact on Tyneside.

Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny.

Bizarrely, Newcastle have lost 22 of their past 33 Premier League matches on a Monday and many of their supporters headed for the exits well before the final whistle on a miserable rainy night.

Barry's eighth goal this season, including four in his past six matches, gave Everton their second win against Newcastle in the space of five days following their 3-1 victory in the League Cup fourth round on Thursday.

Everton ended their run of two successive league defeats after losing against Arsenal and Chelsea.

It was Everton's first away league win since February 28 when they took three points on their previous visit to Newcastle.

Jack Grealish was absent from the Everton squad for a second successive game after being axed for the Newcastle match last week owing to a "breach of club discipline".

The on-loan Manchester City winger, who has been criticised for his off-field behaviour for much of his colourful career, reportedly skipped training before the League Cup clash.

Everton said he was "not match fit" for the rematch with the Magpies, but his team coped just fine without him.

Newcastle made a lively start and went close when Harvey Barnes fired just wide before Joelinton was narrowly off target from 25 yards.

But chances were at a premium for both sides in a scrappy first half more notable for perspiration than inspiration.

Everton's opener four minutes after half-time was in keeping with the grimy fare that preceded it.

Newcastle's dismal marking let in Tyrique George for a shot that drew a weak save from Lukas Hornicek.

Hornicek could only push it straight into the path of Barry for a simple tap-in that survived a lengthy VAR check for offside.

It was a chance so easy that even the notoriously erratic Barry couldn't fail to hit the target, although Newcastle were aggrieved by the VAR decision to let it stand.

Fabian Schar wasted a good opportunity to equalise when he blazed wide.

And Jaissle's men came within a whisker of levelling through Anthony Elanga, whose close-range shot clipped the post and rolled along the goalline before Everton scrambled it clear.

Summing up their inconsistent display, it took 86 minutes for Newcastle to finally register a shot on target and even then Yoane Wissa's effort was routine for Pickford.

Wissa did manage to force a better save from Pickford in stoppage time.

But Ramsey saw red for two bookings in the space of 60 seconds to complete Newcastle's misery. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Trump says midterms most important 'in our lifetime'
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump on Monday chose the backdrop of Washington's Reflecting Pool – a landmark whose botched renovation symbolised…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Monday chose the backdrop of Washington's Reflecting Pool – a landmark whose botched renovation symbolised the 80-year-old's chaotic second term – to try and rally Republicans against a predicted Democratic win in the midterms.

"This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime," Trump said 26 minutes into a rambling speech that focused on his project to renovate monuments in the US capital, rather than inflation, the Iran war and other issues driving voters.

Polls show Democrats are poised to seize the House of Representatives and within reach of the Senate in Tuesday's vote – a shift that would impose the first real political constraints on the president since he took office nearly two years ago.

Americans are increasingly dissatisfied with the economy, while Trump's own approval ratings have hit record lows.

But a tired-sounding Trump repeatedly veered in the speech to his passion for renovating the Reflecting Pool and other Washington landmarks.

"This project should be a project that unites all Americans," Trump said.

The pool is one of the US capital's historic stages, most famous as the setting for Martin Luther King's "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963 from the steps of the adjacent Lincoln Memorial.

Trump said on Sunday he picked the site "just to show how beautiful it is". But his roughly US$15 million renovation ran into repeated and embarrassing setbacks that he has blamed – without evidence – on saboteurs.

Trump has predicted victory in the midterms for his Republicans, but acknowledged that he could face a new reality in an interview released on Monday by the New York Post's Pod Force One podcast.

"I think we're going to do great – but if we didn't win, I veto everything," he said. "I'll be vetoing, vetoing. And then they'll come along and we'll probably make some deals along the way."

Winning just the House would give Democrats voting power over the federal budget and control of committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues.

A Democratic Senate could also block Trump's lifetime appointments to the courts, including the Supreme Court.

Democrats geared up for final rallies in battleground states, including in Texas with James Talarico and in Kansas with Adam Hamilton – two star Senate candidates seeking major upsets. Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century and Texas is a deep Republican stronghold.

Even so, Democrats remain wary of predicting victory.

Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN that the mood was "nauseously optimistic."

Republicans have run a scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and branding Abdul El-Sayed, the Muslim Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, a terrorist.

Democrats have faced late divisions of their own, with left-wing candidates at times clashing with the party establishment.

On Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, in Michigan's pivotal Senate race. Stevens lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite establishment backing.

While the House appears highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is far closer.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. To win, Democrats must flip seats in states that Trump carried by double digits two years ago.

Forecaster Decision Desk HQ has Democrats winning the Senate 52-48 and the House by a comfortable 241-194.

The final New York Times/Siena poll, released on Sunday evening, showed Democrats leading in all seven of the most competitive Senate races, though five were within the margin of error.

Tuesday is election day, but a record 54 million people have already cast ballots.

The midterms have also drawn about US$11 billion in advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.

Elon Musk, the Trump ally who led the so-called Doge drive to slash the federal government, has given nearly half a billion US dollars to help elect Republicans. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Anthropic says revenue surged 1,100pc ahead of IPO
articles.excerpt: Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly…
articles.fullText:
Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly revenue and nearly US$900 billion in spending commitments as it counts down to its Wall Street listing later this month.

The San Francisco-based company was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers led by chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela, now its president, with AI safety as its focus.

The listing comes amid growing nervousness among investors about the huge sums being poured into AI.

Revenue reached US$17 billion in the third quarter, up from US$1.4 billion a year earlier, though sales growth slowed from previous quarters amid fierce competition from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and cheaper models.

The company, whose stock market debut is seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last, said in an amended filing that its net loss reached US$23.3 billion in the July-September period.

The loss stemmed mostly from non-cash accounting charges linked to the company's rising valuation, the filing showed.

Anthropic also posted an operating loss of US$567 million in the third quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity.

The filing said the company has committed to spend about US$895 billion, mostly on computing power, with US$70 billion of that due before September 2027.

The IPO will be a major test of the market's faith in the AI boom, with the pool of potential investors set to widen as retail traders get their first chance to buy shares directly in a standalone AI giant.

According to several media outlets, the five-year-old company plans to raise around US$100 billion in its initial public offering, at a valuation of between US$1.5 trillion and US$2 trillion.

That would surpass the record set in June by SpaceX, which raised US$86 billion. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: US approves cheap generic HIV shot for poorer nations
articles.excerpt: The US Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved a low-cost version of a twice-yearly HIV prevention shot, bringing the…
articles.fullText:
The US Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved a low-cost version of a twice-yearly HIV prevention shot, bringing the breakthrough drug closer to market in low-income countries.

The tentative approval was announced by Dr Reddy's Laboratories, the Indian maker of the generic version of lenacapavir, and by Unitaid, a global health initiative.

The generic will be available for US$40 per person per year in 120 countries, under a pricing agreement announced in September 2025 between Unitaid, the African health research institute Wits RHI, and the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) and Dr Reddy's.

Lenacapavir was first developed by US pharmaceutical company Gilead Sciences and approved in June 2025 after proving more than 99.9 percent effective in large clinical trials.

"This is an extraordinary milestone for global health. For too long, people in lower- and middle-income countries have had to wait a decade or more to access breakthrough medicines already available elsewhere," said Carmen Perez-Casas, Unitaid's senior strategy lead for HIV and pandemic preparedness.

"With lenacapavir, we've reduced that gap to little more than a year. Having an FDA-approved generic at US$40 per person per year – a price comparable to daily HIV prevention pills – is a remarkable achievement."

A twice-yearly injectable that is akin to a vaccine – albeit without training the immune system – can be a more effective way to administer HIV preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) than daily pills, which first won US approval in 2012 but only work if taken consistently.

But lenacapavir's high cost – roughly $28,000 per year in the US, though insurance lowers what patients pay – was a major obstacle to its becoming a game-changer against a disease that has killed over 40 million people in four decades.

In late 2024, Gilead granted voluntary licenses for lenacapavir to six generic manufacturers, including Dr Reddy's.

Even before generic availability, more than 125,000 people in 10 early adopter African countries have already started Gilead's lenacapavir, Unitaid's statement said.

"This is a moment of immense pride for all of us at Dr Reddy's," said Deepak Sapra, CEO of Pharmaceutical Services and API at Dr Reddy's, in a statement.

The generic was granted "tentative approval" by the FDA, Unitaid said, under an accelerated pathway that allows sponsors to use existing data.

Lenacapavir was named "Breakthrough of the Year" in 2024 by the prestigious journal Science, which hailed the basic research underpinning the drug, specifically a new understanding of HIV's capsid protein, which forms a protective shell around the virus's genetic material and which lenacapavir targets.

An HIV infection once condemned patients to Aids (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome), when the immune system is so damaged that everyday germs make people very sick.

The first antiretrovirals that could fully suppress HIV and stave off Aids were developed in 1996, with current generations even better, allowing people to live normal life spans while managing their chronic infection.

Oral PrEP pills came along in 2012, and before lenacapavir, a PrEP drug called cabotegravir was approved in 2021 requiring shots every two months.

Perez-Casas said the real work for lenacapavir was still ahead, in moving from approval to rollout.

"An estimated 1.2 million people acquired HIV last year, even as we now have a medicine offering near-100 percent protection with just two injections a year," she said.

"The demand is high, and we cannot afford to lose momentum. Unitaid is already working with governments and partners to support country-led rollouts, ensuring that communities play a central role in bringing this breakthrough to the people who need it most." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: UN reports warn of large-scale damage to Earth's ice
articles.excerpt: Exceeding 1.5C of global warming will have "irreversible" consequences for glaciers, sea ice and the Earth's frozen regions, two UN…
articles.fullText:
Exceeding 1.5C of global warming will have "irreversible" consequences for glaciers, sea ice and the Earth's frozen regions, two UN reports warned on Monday, calling for urgent action.

The landmark 2015 Paris Agreement commits the world to limiting warming to well below 2C and pursuing efforts to hold it at 1.5C to try to avoid the worst effects of climate change.

One of the reports said overshooting the 1.5C target "will bring large-scale and in many cases irreversible impacts" for the cryosphere – Earth's ice in all its forms.

Melting of glaciers and sea ice, the thawing of permafrost and the accelerating rise in sea levels, will have widespread repercussions, from flooding to water shortages.

Some of the effects of the rise in temperature are already visible, such as the 20-percent loss in glacial mass in Switzerland.

But even if the 1.5C target remains relevant, it is already too high for the cryosphere, as current levels of warming were "already unsafe" for the Arctic, Antarctic, mountain glaciers and polar oceans, the UN warned.

"Although returning to 1.5 C will slow ice loss, a truly 'safe' temperature for Earth's ice is now thought to be closer to 1C or even below over the coming centuries," it added.

Global warming has already reached 1.37C above pre-industrial levels and according to the European Copernicus network, the 1.5C threshold could be exceeded around 2030.

"There are no good outcomes in exceeding 1.5C," said glaciologist James Kirkham, lead author of one of the reports, entitled "Overshoot and the Cryosphere," which was written with 80 scientists.

"To contain the global fallout and damage from ice loss in the world's polar and mountain regions, overshoot needs to be kept to the absolute minimum," he said.

"Every extra fraction of a degree and every year spent in overshoot means more devastating impacts."

Scientists warn in particular about the risks of crossing certain tipping points and say that, even if temperatures were to return to below the 1.5C threshold, recovery would be very slow.

Reducing warming to under 1.5C and even 1C could see some glaciers partially regenerate, while there could also be benefits for sea ice.

But Matthew England, an oceanographer and climatologist at the University of New South Wales in Australia, said recovery could take "decades to centuries."

The second report – "State of the Cryosphere 2026. The Cost of Overshoot" – shows that exceeding 2.8C into the next century would have significant consequences.

Sea levels could rise by up to five centimetres a year by 2150, compared to the current 0.45 centimetres while the thawing of permafrost could release as much carbon dioxide each year as the United States, the world's second-largest polluter.

A worst-case but not-so-improbable scenario is that the world is heading towards warming of 2.6C by 2100 even if countries meet their climate commitments.

"Temporarily exceeding 1.5C does not mean that the goals of the Paris Agreement are irrelevant but instead makes them more urgent," argued Kirkham.

"Returning to 1.5C or below by 2100 remains possible with sufficient political ambition and urgency, specifically by speeding the transition away from fossil fuel use to reach net zero by mid-century," he said.

"Such urgent action can prevent and even reverse some cryosphere loss."

Gunjan Silwal, a Nepali glacier researcher, said decisions made in the next few years "will lock in the scale of the damage," warning that August's mountain and glacier collapse that killed more than 1,400 and left over 5,000 missing, was "only a foretaste." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
articles.excerpt: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to…
articles.fullText:
In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired.

Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And while most respondents praise the quality of their agents’ descriptive insights, reviews of their prescriptive insights—those on which actions are based—are decidedly mixed.

DOWNLOAD THE REPORT

Failure to produce insights that improve the business deprives organizations of their desired return on investment in agentic analytics. Worse, flawed insights that trigger incorrect actions can cause reputational or financial damage. This report gauges how companies view the quality of the outputs produced by their analytics agents and explores how organizations are seeking to boost insight quality and get their agents working harder for the business.

Some key findings from the report include the following:

Agentic analytics is only just starting to deliver. On average, 48% of insights generated by analytics agents at the surveyed companies lead to actions that improve the business. That is a marked advance from the 37% average the respondents say generated such actions one year ago. But it means that more than half of the insights generated by analytics agents today are still failing to help businesses.

Better quality of insights leads to clear business advantage. At a small cohort of organizations, which we term “insight leaders,” AI agents perform much better than the average. In this group, more than 70% of agent insights lead to actions that improve the business. The insight leaders also give the quality of their agents’ insights higher marks than do the total respondents overall. The quality gap is particularly wide when it comes to prescriptive insights.

Insufficient context reduces insight quality. When analytics agents deliver insights of substandard quality, the main reason is a lack of business context, as cited by 55% of surveyed executives. Fragmented or inaccessible data is the other major factor, according to 45%. Fewer insight leaders say their agents struggle with access to context.

Insight overload further inhibits agent effectiveness. At a majority (52%) of surveyed organizations, analytics agents generate too many insights to be properly evaluated and therefore acted upon. Less than one-quarter (24%) are able to evaluate all agent insights; most do so on a case-by-case basis, and that process is currently human-intensive.

Governance and semantics are areas of focus for improving insights. The surveyed companies are prioritizing initiatives that enable better agent insights by strengthening AI and data governance (cited by 60%). They are also adding a semantic layer to their data architecture (45%). The experts we interviewed agree that the semantic layer is crucial to ensure high-performing agents.

Download the report

This content was produced by Insights, MIT Technology Review’s custom content arm, not its editorial staff. It was researched and written by humans, with any AI tools that may have been used limited to production processes under human oversight.

articles.title: Arbitral hearings scheme extended
articles.excerpt: The Government announced today the expansion of the Immigration Facilitation Scheme for Persons Participating in Arbitral Proceedings in Hong Kong…
articles.fullText:
The Government announced today the expansion of the Immigration Facilitation Scheme for Persons Participating in Arbitral Proceedings in Hong Kong .

The Department of Justice outlined that the new measures provide greater convenience to those covered by the scheme, incentivising them to choose Hong Kong as a place to conduct arbitration and bolstering the city's competitiveness as an arbitral seat.

The Government said that since its regularisation last year, the scheme has been welcomed by the legal and dispute resolution sector and the international arbitration community, adding that its facilitation of international and cross-border arbitral proceedings in Hong Kong has strengthened the city’s position as a premier international arbitration hub.

The scheme's expansion means it now covers arbitral proceedings that occur physically, or in hybrid fashion, in Hong Kong, and are administered by dispute resolution institutions or permanent offices set up in the Chinese Mainland, Macao, Taiwan or overseas, supported by a designated arbitral and dispute resolution institution in Hong Kong under the "Arrangement Concerning Mutual Assistance in Court-ordered Interim Measures in Aid of Arbitral Proceedings by the Courts of the Mainland and of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region".

The Governement explained that "supported by" means that such an institution will provide venue, hearing or meeting facilities, in addition to ancillary services, such as those provided by tribunal reporters and interpreters, translators and caterers, to support arbitrations.

For proceedings newly covered under the scheme's expansion, arbitral and dispute resolution institutions offering support are required to verify the identities of participants in arbitral proceedings.

articles.title: Growth estimated at 5.2% in Q3
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's economy is estimated to have grown 5.2% year on year in the third quarter, up from a 4.2%…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong's economy is estimated to have grown 5.2% year on year in the third quarter, up from a 4.2% increase in the second quarter.

The Census & Statistics Department released its advance estimates of gross domestic product (GDP) for the third quarter today.

On a seasonally adjusted quarter-to-quarter comparison basis, real GDP increased by 1.9% in the third quarter.

The Government said the Hong Kong economy expanded robustly from July through September, underpinned by accelerating growth in exports and solid domestic demand.

It added that, for the first three quarters combined, real GDP grew by 5.1% over a year earlier, the fastest growth for the corresponding period in five years.

Looking ahead, the Government said Hong Kong’s economic outlook remains positive, with incoming data pointing to sustained growth momentum.

However, it added that persistent uncertainties in the external environment, particularly developments surrounding geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and tighter monetary policies from many major central banks, warrant close monitoring.

articles.title: LawTech funding scheme launched
articles.excerpt: The Department of Justice (DoJ) today officially launched the Funding Scheme for LawTech Solution Subscription by the Hong Kong Legal…
articles.fullText:
The Department of Justice (DoJ) today officially launched the Funding Scheme for LawTech Solution Subscription by the Hong Kong Legal Sector, aiming to boost the local legal sector’s technological capability and fortify the city’s status as an international legal and dispute resolution hub.

The scheme is a policy initiative under the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address. It will be jointly managed by the Hong Kong Bar Association and the Law Society of Hong Kong , which will handle applications and disburse funds.

Applications are open from today until January 29, 2027. Eligible applicants include sole practitioners, Hong Kong law firms with no more than five partners, and barristers with no more than seven years of call.

Deputy Secretary for Justice and Chairman of the Consultation Group on LawTech Development Cheung Kwok-kwan stated that promoting LawTech is a core DoJ policy initiative. He noted that since last year, the DoJ has hosted five rounds of the LexGoTech Roundtables to gather feedback from practitioners, academics and stakeholders.

He added that the DoJ is aware that small and medium-sized law firms, as well as junior barristers, are particularly concerned about the financial burden of adopting LawTech tools. The scheme is launched to directly respond to the industry’s needs.

He pointed out that small and medium-sized law firms account for about 88% of all law firms in Hong Kong, while junior barristers with less than seven years of call make up about one-third of the total practicing bar. The scheme will lower the barrier to entry and enhance the overall competitiveness of Hong Kong's legal sector.

Operating on an actual-expense reimbursement basis, the scheme provides up to $20,000 per applicant for a one-year subscription. Applicants can choose from a designated list of 14 local, Mainland and overseas providers covering legal research, document drafting, workflow management and hearing support.

To ensure effectiveness, these service providers will offer transparent pricing alongside technical support and training. The application process consists of four steps.

First, applicants must select a provider from the designated list and obtain a written price quotation. Second, they will submit their application to either the Hong Kong Bar Association or the Law Society of Hong Kong.

Third, the relevant body will issue a written result, after which successful applicants can subscribe to their chosen service. Finally, applicants submit proof of subscription and payment to their respective professional body to claim reimbursement.

articles.title: DC member sentenced to prison
articles.excerpt: The District Court today sentenced Yuen Long District Council (DC) Member Sei Chun-hing to 2.5 years’ imprisonment following his conviction…
articles.fullText:
The District Court today sentenced Yuen Long District Council (DC) Member Sei Chun-hing to 2.5 years’ imprisonment following his conviction for unlawful intercourse with a girl under 16.

Under the District Councils Ordinance, any DC member convicted of an offence and sentenced to a prison term exceeding three months without the option of a fine is disqualified from holding office.

As both the prosecution and the defence retain the right to lodge an appeal, the Government will closely monitor the developments of the judicial proceedings.

Meanwhile, Mr Sei's remuneration package as a DC member has been suspended since his conviction on September 14.

The Government places great importance on the conduct and integrity of DC members.

In accordance with the ordinance and the performance monitoring system of DC members, the Secretary for Home & Youth Affairs has appointed a supervisory committee to conduct an investigation. The committee will follow up on the matter as the case develops.

articles.title: CE begins Beijing visit
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee today arrived in Beijing, where he began his visit by touring the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee today arrived in Beijing, where he began his visit by touring the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center and meeting officials.

At the centre, Mr Lee visited the Beijing Library and the planning exhibition hall at the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee building. He learned about the overall planning, development and construction of cultural facilities at the centre.

The Chief Executive remarked that the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center is one of the capital's “two wings” in the co-ordinated development of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. He observed that this blueprint promotes higher-quality development and demonstrates the country's forward-looking and systemic deployment.

Mr Lee highlighted that Hong Kong is advancing at full steam with the development of the Northern Metropolis (NM), adding that the centre's experience in aspects spanning overall planning and development, supporting infrastructure, and the layout of public service facilities, can be instructive for Hong Kong in the NM's development.

He later met CPC Beijing Municipal Committee Secretary Yin Li and Beijing Mayor Yin Yong to exchange views on deepening co-operation between Hong Kong and Beijing. Executive Deputy Director of the Hong Kong & Macao Work Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council's Hong Kong & Macao Affairs Office Xu Qifang were also present.

The Chief Executive said that Beijing and Hong Kong have always maintained close co-operation, adding that they have strengthened collaboration through the Hong Kong/Beijing Co-operation Conference mechanism.

He outlined that the annual Beijing Hong Kong Economic Co-operation Symposium, held alternately in the two places, is a platform for deepening bilateral economic and trade co-operation and promoting high-level mutual benefits.

Mr Lee added: “The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government announced Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan in September to proactively align with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and deepen regional co-operation with the Mainland.”

He said he looked forward to Hong Kong and Beijing continuing to complement each other's strengths, strengthen collaboration, and promote higher-level co-operation to serve the country's high-quality development.

The Chief Executive also mentioned that the Hong Kong SAR Government is advancing the establishment of “four centres and one hub”, and extending the Cross-sectoral Professional Services Platform to help Mainland enterprises "go global" and attract international capital to Hong Kong.

He urged more Mainland enterprises, including those from Beijing, to make use of Hong Kong's international professional capabilities, its open capital market, and its roles as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" to flexibly meet the needs of their target markets and explore new business opportunities.

He added that the Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to expand youth development work between the two places, thereby supporting young people in seizing the opportunities presented by national development and enabling Hong Kong to better integrate into and serve that development.

Tomorrow, Mr Lee is scheduled to attend the opening ceremony of the 29th Beijing Hong Kong Economic Co-operation Symposium and deliver a speech. He will then depart for Shanghai.

articles.title: September retail sales up 6.4%
articles.excerpt: The total value of retail sales in September, provisionally estimated at $33.4 billion, was up 6.4% compared with the same…
articles.fullText:
The total value of retail sales in September, provisionally estimated at $33.4 billion, was up 6.4% compared with the same month a year earlier, the Census & Statistics Department said today.

After netting out the effect of price changes over the same period, the provisional estimate of the volume of total retail sales represents a 3.9% year-on-year increase.

Online sales accounted for 13.1% of the total retail sales value in September. Provisionally estimated at $4.4 billion, the value of this segment rose 12% from the same month a year earlier.

The value of sales of electrical goods and other consumer durable goods not elsewhere classified increased by 9.7% in September 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier.

There were also increases in the following categories: jewellery, watches and clocks, and valuable gifts (up 20.3%); other consumer goods not elsewhere classified (up 11.5%); food, alcoholic drinks and tobacco (up 5.3%); medicines and cosmetics (up 9%); wearing apparel (up 11.1%); footwear, allied products and other clothing accessories (up 12.4%); furniture and fixtures (up 9%); and optical shops (up 14.6%).

Meanwhile, the value of sales of commodities in supermarkets dropped by 1% in September 2026 over a year earlier. This was followed by sales of commodities in department stores (down 4.1%); books, newspapers, stationery and gifts (down 0.5%); fuels (down 3.1%); motor vehicles and parts (down 34.7%); and Chinese drugs and herbs (down 3%).

The Government said total retail sales value grew at a faster year-on-year rate in September, marking the 17th consecutive month of expansion. It noted that growth in sales was broad-based across many types of retail outlets, reflecting solid local consumption sentiment in general.

A pick-up in visitor arrivals and sales of festive items associated with the earlier arrival of Mid-Autumn Festival this year also contributed to growth in overall sales in the month. Meanwhile, online retail sales value rose further alongside consumers' growing use of digital channels.

Looking ahead, the Government said that sustained solid economic expansion and growth in labour earnings will bolster local consumption. A series of upcoming mega-events and festive celebrations in various districts, together with continued growth in inbound tourism, will inject additional momentum into the retail sector.

articles.title: Removal of Winnie Ho approved
articles.excerpt: The Central People's Government has approved the removal of Winnie Ho from her post as Secretary for Housing, following a…
articles.fullText:
The Central People's Government has approved the removal of Winnie Ho from her post as Secretary for Housing, following a recommendation by Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Chief Executive John Lee. The announcement was made in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong SAR of the People's Republic of China.

Mr Lee noted that Ms Ho tendered her resignation last Wednesday to assume political accountability for the Wang Fuk Court fire.

Ms Ho joined the Government in 1992 and was appointed Director of Architectural Services in 2020. She assumed the role of Secretary for Housing in 2022, becoming a principal official of the sixth-term of the Hong Kong SAR Government.

The Chief Executive commended Ms Ho for her dedication to implementing his key housing directives. These included the construction of around 30,000 Light Public Housing units and successfully shortening the Composite Waiting Time for Subsidised Rental Housing from 6.1 years to 4.8 years.

Mr Lee also praised her for effectively combating the abuse of public rental housing and enacting the Basic Housing Units Ordinance to phase out substandard subdivided residential units in an orderly manner.

As Ms Ho officially leaves office today, Mr Lee wishes her good health and the very best in her future endeavours.

articles.title: October property sales fall 10%
articles.excerpt: The Land Registry logged 5,795 sale and purchase agreements received for registration for all building units in October, a decrease…
articles.fullText:
The Land Registry logged 5,795 sale and purchase agreements received for registration for all building units in October, a decrease of 10% compared with September and down 19.4% year on year.

The total consideration for building unit sale and purchase agreements in October dropped 6.5% from the previous month to $50 billion, representing a 13.6% year-on-year decrease.

A total of 4,512 agreements were for residential units, down 5.2% from the previous month and down 21% from a year ago.

The total consideration for residential units was $42.3 billion, a decrease of 9.5% compared with the previous month and a drop of 17.1% year on year.

There were 418,352 land register searches last month.

articles.title: 5 HK universities in Asia's top 10
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau said today that Hong Kong’s higher education institutions had delivered a stellar performance in the “World University…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau said today that Hong Kong’s higher education institutions had delivered a stellar performance in the “World University Rankings: Asia 2027” published by Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), an international higher education research organisation.

The bureau said that overall the sector had once again demonstrated outstanding international competitiveness and academic excellence within Asia.

It added that the results reflect the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government’s sustained commitment to investing resources and its proactive initiatives in supporting higher education development, which have consolidated the city’s position as an international post-secondary education hub.

In the latest rankings, the University of Hong Kong retained the top spot in Asia.

A total of five Hong Kong universities are among Asia’s top 10, with three of these ranking in the top five: besides the University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong ranked fourth, with the Chinese University of Hong Kong sitting in fifth.

Eight local universities improved their rankings this year, with all 11 ranked Hong Kong institutions featuring among the top 500 in Asia. The bureau said this demonstrates a comprehensive elevation in the quality of Hong Kong’s higher education.

At the same time, Hong Kong universities continue to lead Asia in key indicators such as academic reputation, employer reputation, internationalisation, and research impact.

The bureau also highlighted that the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026 will be inaugurated tomorrow.

A premier international education event, the forum brings together university presidents, distinguished scholars, and international education leaders from dozens of world-class institutions to deliberate on issues such as talent cultivation in the intelligent era, the role of technology and innovation in driving the future economy, and universities’ responses to major global challenges.

The Hong Kong SAR Government said it will continue to support local universities in reaching new heights and enhance the international leadership of Hong Kong’s higher education sector through various policies and measures. These include advancing the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town, attracting top international research talent and students, and deepening cross-boundary and international academic collaborations.

articles.title: New fridge cyberattack hits Belgium stores
articles.excerpt: Dozens of Belgian grocery stores and an Ikea superstore saw their refrigerator temperatures soar on Monday, with several of the…
articles.fullText:
Dozens of Belgian grocery stores and an Ikea superstore saw their refrigerator temperatures soar on Monday, with several of the firms involved confirming they had been hit by a cyberattack.

It is the latest in a series of cyberattacks on store refrigerators and suspicious actions around the supermarkets across Europe.

A handful of Swedish supermarkets saw temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers soar early on Monday, Swedish chains Ica and Coop said without giving a cause. Major French retailers said on October 12 that hundreds of store refrigeration systems were hit by a cyberattack, which forced them to throw out spoiled food and raised food security fears.

Carrefour Belgium reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium. "It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," said Mich Vergauwen, a spokesman for Carrefour Belgium.

An Ikea Belgium spokeswoman likewise said a cyberattack hit its store in Mons, southwestern Belgium, causing the temperature of freezers to rise suddenly in the early hours of Monday.

It is the only Ikea store affected because it uses a different service provider than others in Belgium, the spokeswoman added, without identifying the provider.

The Delhaize supermarket chain meanwhile said refrigeration systems in "dozens" of its stores were affected by an IT incident.

The Colruyt and Intermarche supermarket chains likewise said they had been hit by technical problems affecting fridges in five and around 15 stores respectively, without confirming if a cyberattack was suspected.

"In some cases, it involved only a single refrigerator, so the impact was quite limited," an Intermarche spokesman said, adding that the incidents took place overnight Sunday-to-Monday.

The issue is not limited to Belgium.

The Swedish chains ICA and Coop said they were looking into the cause of their temperature soars that forced them to throw away food.

One ICA store at Sjobo in southern Sweden, posted on Facebook, however, that its fridges and freezers had "been hacked and they set the temperature at 50 degrees" Celsius.

More than 500 supermarkets were targeted in the French attack on October 12. The equipment was provided by Danish company, Danfoss. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Three-vehicle crash in Tsuen Wan injures nine
articles.excerpt: Nine people sustained light injuries in a car crash involving three vehicles in Tsuen Wan on Monday night. Police said…
articles.fullText:
Nine people sustained light injuries in a car crash involving three vehicles in Tsuen Wan on Monday night.

Police said they were alerted at 7.30pm that a minibus collided with a private vehicle and a light goods vehicle on Tsuen Wan Road.

The collision shattered the minibus' windshield.

All of those hurt were conscious.

A part of Tsuen Wan Road was temporarily closed due to the incident.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Foreign firms debut in HK to access mainland market
articles.excerpt: A number of foreign companies have made their debut at the annual Hong Kong Fintech Week and StartmeupHK that commenced…
articles.fullText:
A number of foreign companies have made their debut at the annual Hong Kong Fintech Week and StartmeupHK that commenced on Monday, hoping to use the SAR as a springboard to tap into the mainland market.

They include a Canadian company that produces renewable fuels.

Jag Singh from SBI BioEnergy noted that his firm can contribute to the SAR’s green aviation development, and hopes to also explore opportunities in the mainland market.

“Everyone in the world has a shortage of sustainable aviation fuel and a target to blend sustainable aviation fuel,” he said.

“So we are helping to achieve that and we can do it globally because it's our own process modular, and we have all the control of the technology because we have the hydrogen production as well as the conversion system in them.”

Singh went on to say that the firm’s next goal is to expand even further in Asia through Hong Kong.

"We hear a lot about the great agreements and structures here and IP protection, and that's very important to us because these are our babies – these are our patented processes – we spent a lot of time and blood, sweat and tears to make this happen," he said.

"So I think it’s a perfect gateway or potential base as a springboard to the rest of Asia and China."

Canadian firm Deep Sky, which specialises in carbon removal, is also taking part in the event.

“What I’ve noticed is there's an incredible density of companies that are developing energy infrastructure in [the] mainland and internationally, financiers financing those projects and trading firms who are trading the products,” the firm's Charlie Renzoni said.

“So I see an incredibly important connection between Hong Kong, [the] mainland and the rest of the world.”

For Korean firm MoneyStation, which focuses on AI-powered investment intelligence, they decided to make the SAR their first stop to go overseas.

“Hong Kong is like a pioneer in adapting the new financial business models like cryptos or stock markets and asset management,” its founder James Lee said.

He added that the city’s annual event also offered them a chance to look for strategic business partners.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: 'HK crucial for mainland firms' global expansion'
articles.excerpt: Mainland companies have hailed the city’s annual flagship finance and technology event, saying it offers an opportunity for them to…
articles.fullText:
Mainland companies have hailed the city’s annual flagship finance and technology event, saying it offers an opportunity for them to carry out exchanges with potential overseas partners.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Hong Kong Fintech Week and StartmeupHK on Monday, Liu Yong from the Zhongguancun Fintech Industry Development said this year was their third time participating in the event.

He said that the SAR’s role as a super connector was crucial for the mainland in setting up shop overseas.

“Hong Kong can fully leverage its strength in international talent. Because in the international aspects, such as accounting standards, Hong Kong itself is an international financial centre – it has a very good foundation and conditions,” he said.

Mu Rong from the Greater Bay Area fintech delegation noted that some firms focusing on securities and asset management, which used to adopt a wait-and-see approach, have gradually set up shop in Hong Kong to start doing business overseas.

“Some of these tech companies have started making profits. The orders that they received from overseas customers were even larger than those from the mainland,” she said.

“This shows that Hong Kong fully recognised their technical capabilities.”

Mu went on to say that firms that wish to expand to international markets will now team up, rather than go it alone.

Wang Yu, who represented a delegation led by the Union of Finance Alumni of Peking University said that more than 30 percent of the firms in their group – particularly those focusing on AI – are determined to expand globally via the SAR.

Wang highlighted how Hong Kong’s convenience across various aspects, including culture and language, makes it an ideal platform to go global.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
articles.excerpt: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates…
articles.fullText:
When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive.

The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code. GitHub Copilot moved from flat-rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner predicts that AI coding token costs will surpass average developer salaries by 2028.

The natural response is rationing usage caps, seat limits, and approvals before developers launch agents. But blanket limits can restrict the workflows delivering value. They also optimize the wrong number. Cost per token measures consumption, not results. Some spending reflects waste, including retries and runaway loops. Some represents the work of shipping software. A meter cannot distinguish them, and neither can a spending cap.

Measure the software that ships

A better measure is cost per merged pull request: total AI-assisted development cost divided by the number of changes that pass review and are merged. Track rework and defects alongside it so cheaper changes do not conceal lower quality.

If that cost falls as AI usage rises, without compromising quality, developers are converting more consumption into useful software. The question is not how many tokens they use, but how much finished work the investment produces.

Improving that equation requires two changes: reserve expensive inference for tasks that need it, and lower the cost of routine work.

Match the model to the task

Agentic coding does not require the most powerful model at every step. Use a frontier model, or an on-premises flagship when policy requires it, for difficult planning and novel reasoning. Route suitable work, including code generation, test creation, and repeated refactoring, to open-weight models you operate yourself.

A gateway can route requests according to task complexity, data sensitivity, cost, and latency. This reserves premium inference for the moments that justify it rather than applying premium pricing to an entire workflow. Meter the exception, not the workload.

Open-weight models make this division increasingly practical. Software-engineering benchmarks show that leading open-weight models can approach frontier performance on some tasks. That does not establish equivalence across every repository or workflow. Evaluate candidates against your own code, tests, and acceptance criteria before assigning production work.

Change the economics of repeated use

Next, decide who owns the capacity. With rented inference, every call adds to the bill. With owned capacity, most of the cost is committed upfront, so each additional call gets cheaper as usage grows.

The economics are simple: per-token pricing makes heavy use more expensive, while owned capacity becomes more efficient as teams use it more. Ownership is not free, though. Power, operations, maintenance, and depreciation all must be considered. The number that matters is the fully loaded cost per merged pull request.

Owned capacity also delivers a type of value that never appears on an invoice: control over sensitive code. When code generation and testing run on-premises, proprietary code stays inside the enterprise. Only approved planning prompts and governed exceptions go to external models, through a gateway the organization controls. That opens the sensitive repositories where security usually stalls adoption, and where the biggest gains are waiting.

Test the operating model

At HPE, a hybrid AI platform routes routine workloads from more than 150 internal applications to open-weight models running on premises, including on HPE Private Cloud AI. The result: token costs down 30 to 50%.

That is the point of hybrid. With HPE Private Cloud AI, owning your inference does not mean giving up frontier models. Run the volume on capacity you own and let a gateway send the hardest work.

Data also shows that usage, not licensed headcount, drives spend. The top 5% of users generated most of the consumption, and the heaviest used roughly 450 times more than the lightest on the same license. If power users grow from a small minority to half the workforce, monthly spend can rise about 4.4 times with flat headcount. Your mix will differ, which is exactly why you need to measure it.

HPE tracks two metrics and recommends customers do the same. First, it tracks cost per active developer, because averaging across all licenses hides the power users driving spend. Second, it tracks cost per merged pull request, because it connects AI spending to software that ships.

Baseline both costs before changing infrastructure. Then run a complete development cycle on owned capacity. If both metrics do not improve as usage grows, your current model may still be the better choice.

Build for adoption, not rationing

Owned capacity is not for everyone. Low or unpredictable usage favors APIs, with no capital tied up in idle infrastructure. Ownership pays off when sustained demand keeps it busy. Most enterprises will run hybrid: frontier APIs for demanding or intermittent work, owned capacity for repeatable volume. A governed gateway decides what leaves the building, so you get frontier models without giving up sovereignty over your code.

As developers lean harder on coding agents, usage will keep rising. The real choice is whether that growth shows up as a bigger variable-cost bill or as more software shipped on capacity you own. The companies that lead AI-assisted development will not ration adoption to control costs. They will build an operating model where more AI use improves the economics instead of undermining them.

articles.title: The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

The agentic web is here

In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.

At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts.

This new era is being called the agentic web. It will inevitably transform the internet—and whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess.

Find out how AI agents are transforming the internet, and what we stand to lose in the process .

—Grace Huckins

Are we there yet? Eliminating traffic deaths

Every year, traffic crashes kill more than 1 million people worldwide. They’re also the leading cause of death for children and young adults. Cheap, proven ways to make roads safer exist, including tightening intersections with planters and lowering speed limits. But government logjams and red tape can make it difficult to roll out these changes.

Still, some cities are making impressive progress by investing in public transit, extending curbs, and using cameras to spot danger zones in need of a redesign.

Here’s how close we are to eradicating traffic deaths .

—Sara Kiley Watson

This story is the final part of “Are we there yet?” , our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. Subscribe to read the other five instalments in our new Impossible issue .

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 A $1 trillion tech selloff has deepened fears of an AI bubble
Big AI bills and weak earnings have spooked investors. ( BBC )
+ The Nasdaq 100 had its worst day since June on Friday. ( NBC News )
+ OpenAI has cut its funding target by $10 billion. ( CNBC )
+ What even is the AI bubble? ( MIT Technology Review )

2 Hackers have hit Ukraine and Russia’s emergency alert apps
Kyiv residents were warned of “nuclear danger.” ( NBC News )
+ Russia’s app said nuclear warheads had been launched. ( CNN )
+ Ukraine has blamed Russia, which hasn’t yet accused anyone. ( BI )
+ AI will transform cyber warfare. ( MIT Technology Review )

3 Binance users withdrew $3.6 billion after the largest ever crypto hack
The funds moved when the exchange reopened on Sunday. ( Guardian )
+ Binance says it’s covered $6 billion of the stolen $6.3 billion. ( Reuters $)
+ But the industry’s response has undermined its “decentralized” image. ( Gizmodo )

4 An AI agent injected drugs into a live mouse’s brain
It chose the gene therapy and controlled the needle itself. ( Wired $)
+ We need real-time tracking of AI agents. ( MIT Technology Review )

5 Data centres have made utilities a flashpoint in the midterms
Americans are angry over rising electricity bills. ( Reuters $)
+ Virtual power plants could help. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Apple has overtaken Nvidia as the world’s most valuable company
Investors are favouring its restraint on AI spending. ( Bloomberg $)
+ But critics say it’s entering its “slop era.” ( 404 Media )

7 Supermarket fridges have overheated in a new wave of cyberattacks
Stores in Belgium, Sweden, and Luxembourg were hit. ( Politico )

8 The first chocolate bars made from lab-grown cocoa are here
Startups are cultivating chocolate to tackle a cocoa shortage. ( WSJ $)

9 Hackers hijacked digital billboards in multiple countries to show porn
They also criticized security flaws and Egypt’s government.( Gizmodo )

10 A new 3D map reveals instability in interstellar space
The discovery could help explain why stars form so inefficiently. ( Quanta )

Quote of the day

“It would be great if all this was just a house of cards.”

—Kevin Roose, a technology columnist at the New York Times, tells NPR that an AI investment crash would be preferable to the technology permanently upending work and society.

One more thing

Useful quantum computing is inevitable—and increasingly imminent

Last year, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang jolted the stock market by saying that practical quantum computing is still 15 to 30 years away. He also suggested that those computers would need Nvidia GPUs to function. But Huang’s predictions miss the mark—both on the timeline and the role his company’s technology will play.

Quantum computing is rapidly converging on utility. And that’s good news, because the hope is that they will be able to perform calculations that no amount of AI or classical computation could ever achieve. Read the full story .

—Peter Barrett

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ A miniaturist has built a delightful diorama of the world’s creepiest living room .
+ The year’s best dog photos have been announced, and they’re very good boys and girls.
+ At the Green Zone golf club , you tee off in Sweden and putt in Finland, an hour in the future.
+ Astronomers say they’ve found the real celestial arrangement that inspired van Gogh’s The Starry Night .

articles.title: Beijing working to ease Middle East situation: Wang Yi
articles.excerpt: Wang Yi, the nation's top diplomat, met with Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council in…
articles.fullText:
Wang Yi, the nation's top diplomat, met with Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council in Beijing on Monday.

Wang said that China will follow the initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on easing the situation in the Middle East.

Beijing will also work together with all parties continuously to restore regional peace, he said.

"China supports Iran in safeguarding its own sovereignty and security," he told Bagheri Kani, according to a statement from Beijing.

"All parties should... in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict," Wang added.

China is to send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as a part of "shuttle diplomacy visits... aimed at promoting peace talks [and] easing tensions", a Foreign Ministry spokesperson told a regular news briefing.

Earlier, President Xi had said the Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry. (Xinhua/AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Apple iPhone pre-sales linked to 1,700 fraud cases
articles.excerpt: Police have received more than 1,700 reports of suspected credit-card fraud cases linked to Apple's recent iPhone pre-sales in September…
articles.fullText:
Police have received more than 1,700 reports of suspected credit-card fraud cases linked to Apple's recent iPhone pre-sales in September and October.

At a Southern District Council meeting on Monday, Police Commissioner Joe Chow said the force received 1,589 reports of unauthorised credit card transactions involving the purchase of various Apple iPhone 18 models.

Pre-orders for the smartphone began on September 12 in Hong Kong.

Another 138 reports were filed in October, when the iPhone Duo began accepting orders.

According to Chow, Apple opted against extra security measures for credit card transactions. An example would be the "3D Secure" protocol, which asks customers to enter a one-time password or verify their identity on the bank's mobile app.

"During this period, we contacted Apple, credit card companies and banks, and cancelled all problematic purchase records. As a result, the victims did not suffer any losses," Chow said.

The police chief said officers had reached out to Apple on multiple occasions to express hope that the company would implement effective security measures and strengthen verification in future product launches.

Chow also briefed district councillors on Hong Kong's law-and-order situation.

He said fraud remained the dominant crime category, with 34,679 cases in the first nine months of the year, making up 51 percent of all crimes.

Victims reported losses of HK$6.02 billion, a 6.7 percent increase year on year.

Phone scams were now the most common type of fraud, followed by online shopping deception.

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: Mideast not battleground for great-power rivalry: Xi
articles.excerpt: The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry and Beijing is willing to work…
articles.fullText:
The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry and Beijing is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.

China has traditionally played a low-key diplomatic role in the Middle East but has stepped up efforts to try to help end tensions amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has snarled the Strait of Hormuz and driven up global energy and shipping costs.

Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the world is undergoing profound changes.

"The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all parties," Xi said, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

China has consistently been committed to stopping the war and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas", he added.

It is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.

In a 20-point joint statement, both sides said they agree that normal and safe navigation should resume in the Strait of Hormuz. The countries also called for the US and Iran to pursue peaceful options, return to the agreement struck in June aimed at ending the conflict and restart dialogue.

The ministry said later on Monday that Zhai Jun, its special envoy to the Middle East, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by an Omani head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.

He told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.

"We believe that development and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law – an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."

He also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China.

"We are confident that such an agreement would open new avenues for trade and investment, facilitate and enhance commercial and investment exchanges between our two nations," Haitham said.

China is Oman's largest trade partner, with tourism and business links boosted by direct flights between Beijing and Muscat since November.

Oman, which exports crude oil and energy products to China, has also been looking to further develop its renewable energy supply chains and digital commerce.

Their joint statement said the countries have agreed to deepen practical cooperation in the oil and natural gas sector, as well as expand cooperation in new energy fields such as solar photovoltaics, wind power, power transmission and transformation, and energy storage.

The Omani leader, who was welcomed on the tarmac in Beijing by People's Bank of China governor Pan Gongsheng, also emphasised cooperation between investment and financial institutions. (Reuters)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: The agentic web is here
articles.excerpt: In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two…
articles.fullText:
In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic Web” : an internet designed to be navigated by autonomous software agents that could address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.

To illustrate what this might look like, Berners-Lee and his colleagues told a story about a pair of siblings who use their agents to automatically research and book physical therapy appointments for their mother, making sure they would be covered by insurance and fit their busy calendars.

At the turn of the millennium, this vision seemed far-fetched: Google had only been online for a couple of years, and most people were still on dial-up connections. But a quarter-century on, the dream of autonomous software agents that use the internet and carry out tasks for us has finally been realized. New tools such as Meta’s blockbuster Muse agent, OpenAI’s Dots, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet are being given access to people’s email inboxes and bank accounts,  Meanwhile, in a series of worrying incidents, agents created by OpenAI broke free of their sandboxes and caused havoc online.  

Just as the rise of smartphones sparked the development of a more atomized and attention-grabbing internet, the advent of powerful AI systems heralds a new era: We’re facing not the semantic web but the agentic web. This new web is developing out of sight and in ways that might not be entirely within our control. As it grows, the agentic web will inevitably transform the human web—and whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess.

For Berners-Lee’s original vision to work, internet users would have had to annotate the pages they built with special tags so that a software agent could understand each element’s meaning—say, “street address” for the part of a physical therapy office’s web page that indicates its location and “appointment types” for the list of services. And so the idea never really caught on. “It’s a lot of labor,” says Eni Mustafaraj, a professor of computer science at Wellesley College. “And the benefits of that were not obvious.” For the next two decades, then, the internet remained a place that put humans first, with the odd Twitter reply bot or web scraper to round things out.

Large language models changed that. Unlike the agents that Berners-Lee was imagining, today’s LLM-based agents don’t need any tags to understand which part of the text on a clinic’s site is its address and which details the services it offers. They can search for and process text far faster than any human, and agents with multimodal capabilities can even interpret screenshots of websites and click on specific elements such as hyperlinks and drop-down menus.

They’re also just a way more intuitive means of finding information and accomplishing tasks online. Rather than poring over pages of Google results to find a budget-friendly product dupe or a half-remembered meme, why not have Claude or ChatGPT peruse dozens of sites in just a few minutes, guided only by your vague query? Or go one step further and use a personal assistant agent like Muse to hunt down a restaurant reservation or book a flight.

As agents flood online spaces, this new user base is changing the web for good. Time magazine, for instance, is publishing versions of its articles that are easier for agents to parse and has started selling ads targeted at them. Companies from Etsy to Expedia have partnered with the major AI firms to build tools that allow agents to interface seamlessly with their services.

Despite these early efforts, it’s still tough to tell exactly what forms the agentic web will take and how it will change our online experience. Depending on how it’s designed and who controls access to it, we could be in for something that’s as open and customizable as the web of the early 2000s, only far easier to use.
