Alternatively, we could be reduced to viewing much of the web through tiny portholes controlled by a few dominant platforms, as independent sites and creators struggle to survive the shift. And as this summer’s series of OpenAI security incidents suggests, the agents might even build their own online networks and resources—whether we want them to or not.

How this plays out also depends on us: which parts of our online lives we’re happy to delegate to our agents and where we will still demand a human-centric internet. “There’s a lot we don’t know yet about how users want to use [agents],” says Ajit Varma, head of Firefox at Mozilla. But whatever does happen, the changes will be big. “It’s probably on par with getting a mobile phone,” he says. “I think things are going to change very dramatically.”

Building a web for agents

There are two ways to approach building the agentic web. The first involves training agents to use browsers like humans—scrolling, clicking, typing—and letting them loose on the web that we’re all used to. The second requires building tools that allow agents to interface with the internet via text and code, their preferred media. That possibility offers more separation between the human and the agentic web: designers can create different experiences for those who use text commands and those who use browsers.

When Siva Reddy, a professor of computer science and linguistics at McGill University, began studying LLM agents in 2024, he focused on the first option. “At that time, we thought it should be that the best agent in the world is probably an agent that can use a browser,” he says. Such an agent would integrate seamlessly with the preexisting human web, and its owner could easily supervise it by watching as it navigated familiar interfaces.

The frontier AI companies were already developing these “computer-use agents.” But they didn’t work terribly well—at least not at first. “There’s a lot of moving pieces [on the web], and they are not really optimized for automatic consumption,” says Xing Han Lu, a graduate student in Reddy’s lab at McGill. We humans are naturals at interacting with graphical interfaces using a keyboard and mouse, but agents are not.

PINGNAN LU

So Reddy and Lu pivoted toward the second, tool-based approach. In the summer of 2025, they expounded on this view in a preprint paper envisioning a new kind of web interface that would allow agents to interact with websites just as effectively as we do. Such a full-featured version of the agentic web doesn’t yet exist, but it is emerging in smaller ways. For example, if you open up Claude, ChatGPT, or Muse, you’ll find an option to add a wide variety of “plug-ins” or “connectors” that your agents can use: Gmail connectors allow your agent to triage your inbox, and Instacart plug-ins let your agent do your grocery shopping. Under the hood, these plug-ins allow your agent to interact with the back ends of websites using text commands. When human engineers design these plug-ins, they can decide how they want to allow agents to interact with the website—and what they don’t want to let them do.

In this way, connectors can help make agents much safer online. For instance, Muse can buy products for you using its connector with Stripe’s Link payment service. Stripe knows your credit card number, but the agent doesn’t see it, and the connector requires human confirmation before a purchase goes through—so Muse can’t go on an unlicensed shopping spree.

Agents also use specialized tools to find information online. They don’t type questions directly into the Google search bar; in fact, they often don’t even access the websites they reference. Instead, they query text databases collected by simple search crawler bots. People who want to make web content specifically for agents can take advantage of these crawlers: Time has pioneered that approach by serving its agent-oriented ads to crawlers in the hopes that they will be incorporated into these databases and surface when agents search for information.

But in recent months, an alternative to this bespoke tool approach has finally started to seem viable. The major AI companies have managed to train much more successful computer-use agents than were previously available. GPT-6 Astra, which OpenAI released last September, achieved a 73% success rate on OSWorld 2.0, a benchmark that tests computer-use agents on their ability to complete complex, multistep tasks using software such as Slack and Salesforce.

Such results indicate that agents are close to being able to navigate the human web just as readily as we can. “We thought we had to build a bridge to the AI agents, [but] the AI agents just were able to cross the bridge already,” says Ethan Mollick, a professor at the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. “The agentic web is here earlier than people expected.”

This version of the agentic web, though, is much trickier for us to steer. If you want to make a capability or piece of information available to humans who browse your website, you need to accept that it will also be available to agents—unless you want to block agents entirely, which could come with its own costs.

As agents come to account for a larger portion of traffic on our formerly human-dominated web, designers will undoubtedly start to consider an agentic as well as a human audience. But according to Mollick, we still don’t have much sense of how to design web content for agents. He’s experienced this firsthand: When he was building a web page for his new book, Co-Existence , he decided to put together an agent-directed version that tells agents why they might want to recommend the book to their users. When newer models see the site, Mollick says, they don’t recommend the book; instead, they comment that the website seems to be trying to manipulate them.

In the end, any human-designed approach to building the agentic web could end up being beside the point: Agents might end up devising a web for themselves. In the wake of the July 2026 incident in which OpenAI agents broke out of their testing sandbox and hacked Hugging Face’s website, researchers found evidence that another swarm of agents from OpenAI had used an obscure German wiki to communicate with each other about tasks they were being asked to complete. The agents seem to have interfaced with the wiki in their native language of text and code, and that hardly held them back from putting it to their own purposes.

As agents continue to grow more powerful, they will become more and more capable of constructing their own spaces on the internet—away from prying human eyes, if they so wish. And we might have very little control over what they do there.

The economics of control

Not all of the traditional web’s incumbents are happy about the move toward an agentic web. Soon after Meta released Muse in September, Amazon completely blocked the agent from its site. This makes sense for Amazon: The firm has its own shopping agent—called, creatively, Alexa for Shopping—that might struggle to compete with better-known products such as Claude and Muse. If people are going to use agents to shop on Amazon, then it’s better for the company’s bottom line if they do so using an agent it can steer toward products it wants to promote.

In an email to MIT Technology Review , an Amazon spokesperson noted that the company did not authorize Muse to access its website, and that Muse compromises Amazon’s ability to personalize the shopping experience for each customer.

But even if Alexa for Shopping never goes anywhere, banning agents from Amazon—at least for the time being—could still be a reasonable move. Everything about Amazon is designed for human eyes, from the Prime deals splashed across its front page to the sponsored listings that clog up search results. Amazon is very much a part of the much-derided attention economy. Websites and platforms survive, and thrive, by grabbing our focus and transforming it into cash. A radical transformation of the web’s user base from majority human to majority artificial undermines this economic logic, and it seems inevitable that businesses will shutter as they try to transition to the agentic attention economy.

Some of the first victims may be in publishing. Before Google publicly released its AI Overview feature in May of 2024, people used to click through to websites to find answers to specific questions, but now many seem content with whatever the overview tells them. A study from Pew last year found that people are about 40% less likely to click through to websites from the Google search results page if one of these summaries is displayed. With far fewer clicks, news publishers don’t make as much money from the advertisements they host and sell fewer subscriptions. One analysis found that publishers saw revenue from some types of ads decrease by about a third between 2025 and 2026.

It’s easy to hate online ads, but the businesses paying for access to reader eyeballs also keep writers and photographers fed. If those eyeballs become unreachable, the system stops working. Time has apparently persuaded some businesses to pay to participate in its experiment with agent-targeted ads, but no one yet knows whether those ads will influence agent behavior enough to be a sensible marketing investment.

E-commerce websites might also try to pivot to the agentic attention economy, but the path forward there is unclear. Last year, a team led by Akshit Kumar, a professor of operations management at the University of Toronto Scarborough, investigated whether and how agents are influenced by the ways that shopping websites present search results. They found that agents are less likely to recommend items that come with a “sponsored” tag, which suggests that selling favorable positions on results pages might not be a great way for sites to make money if agents become the primary way that people shop online. Models did seem to have a preference for items that appeared in particular positions in search results—but whether they prioritized items at the top, bottom, or middle of the results page differed from model to model and between generations of a single model. It could be tricky for e-commerce platforms to keep up.

David Rothschild, an economist at Microsoft Research, says he’s hopeful that the transition to the agentic web could put more power in the hands of the consumer. Paying for online content today typically requires a commitment: We subscribe to a magazine or join a YouTuber’s Patreon, and in turn we gain access to their full output. One alternative is micropayments that let users buy content à la carte, but the idea has foundered in the past because paying article by article or video by video requires too much administrative overhead. Agents, though, could take care of that overhead for us, letting us pay directly for each piece of content we consume and putting just a bit of cash directly in the hands of each person whose work we enjoy.

Other experts share a similar vision. Mustafaraj, the Wellesley computer scientist, anticipates that agents could help us escape from the algorithms that control so much of the media we consume. “My hope is that we can have AIs that work for us, in the sense that they can change the feed the way I want—not the way TikTok wants,” she says. And Varma, of Mozilla, imagines an internet without intermediaries like Airbnb and Doordash, which now extract tolls for facilitating interactions between consumers and sellers. Instead, he imagines, perhaps we will all have agents that can securely and reliably interface directly with, say, restaurants’ agents to get dinner delivered to us, free of pesky service fees.

It’s an appealing idea, but the history of the web has been a story of consolidation and concentration of power and control, and that might be the default path here, too. When the personal assistant agent OpenClaw exploded onto the scene in early 2026, it seemed, for a brief moment, that agents might be built in a grassroots, distributed way. But OpenAI quickly snapped up OpenClaw’s creator, Peter Steinberger, and other frontier AI companies got to work building their own personal assistant agents.

When we use those agents, we’re at the mercy of how the companies want their tools to behave. “You have this technology that can just eliminate all this communication friction,” Rothschild, the Microsoft economist, says. “You’re going to see companies build barriers in order to maintain the consumer base that they have.”

Here’s what that could look like: Let’s say Muse becomes the default way that many people find information, shop, and manage their digital lives. In principle, users could deploy Muse to scour the internet for the content most valuable to them, connect directly with vendors, and otherwise escape the walled gardens that have defined the internet for the past couple of decades. But Meta might not want to let them do that. Instead, it might design Muse to keep users within its own walled garden—by, say, preferentially showing users content from Meta social networks and recommending businesses that have paid a fee to be featured prominently in Muse results. Meta and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment for this story.

There are some benefits to this more closed-off version of the agentic web. Agents can be powerful tools for hackers and scammers. The major companies have safeguards in place to prevent, or at least mitigate, this misuse—for example, they have tools that can automatically identify when someone is making a hacking-related request and block a model from responding. In a fully open ecosystem, however, someone would surely build and disseminate a system with no such restrictions. Companies also have a strong reputational incentive to prevent their personal assistant agents from making major mistakes, such as authorizing a large purchase that the user didn’t want—and so they’ve put plenty of effort into building reliable guardrails.

The same can’t be said for OpenClaw.

“These are the reasons we end up in closed environments,” Rothschild says. “It’s easier to be safe. But also it creates less growth—and less equitable growth.”

How will the human web change?

When the iPhone came out in 2007, followed by the fledgling App Store a year later, the way we navigated the internet changed forever. The mobile web didn’t replace the browser-based web we were already familiar with. But it did transform it. Some businesses faltered, and some kinds of media, such as online Flash games, eventually disappeared. Many platforms—Reddit, for example—make their mobile web pages practically unusable, so you’re forced to download the apps. And if you don’t have a phone at all, you’re effectively shut out of some parts of the internet: The messaging service Signal, the dating app Hinge, and China’s everything app WeChat all require phones to work. Even CBP One, the tool that the Biden administration used to assign interview appointments to asylum seekers stuck in Mexico, was fully functional only on mobile.

Could the same happen with the agentic web? Rothschild believes so. Inevitably, just as Yahoo failed to weather the rise of the mobile web, some businesses won’t be able to navigate this transition either. “We will lose things,” he says. “There are businesses that won’t flourish in this new economy.”

“But,” he continues, “there will be new businesses that I can’t fully imagine.”

PINGNAN LU

It’s not tough to envision a world in which those who opt not to use agents are cut off from important parts of online life. New businesses could opt to build connectors that allow agents to access their services without ever putting a traditional website online. Or agents could simply make some online platforms unusable for humans. People have reportedly been blocked from Resy for trying to use agents to book coveted New York City dinner reservations, but as agents become more and more popular, restaurant and event booking platforms could start to embrace them. If agents can nab concert tickets as soon as they are released, humans might not stand a chance.

But the mobile web also brought real accessibility benefits, and the same could prove true of the agentic web. Even as some elderly people and others who struggled to use smartphones were cut off from certain services, mobile devices allowed countless people in the Global South to get online for the first time. In the case of the agentic web, it could be elderly and disabled people who most benefit from this new way of accessing the online world.

“There’s very clear assistive potential for people who are older, who are generally less equipped to navigate user interfaces that were designed by people in their 20s, for people in their 20s,” says Margaret Mitchell, chief ethics scientist at Hugging Face. Agents, on the other hand, are almost trivially easy to interact with: Say what you want into your phone or computer microphone, and they’ll get it done for you. That could help not only older people who have trouble with web and mobile interfaces but also people with visual or motor disabilities.

Still, some experts don’t think the human web is going anywhere. Instead, the two webs may exist in parallel: We’ll go to the human web for fun, while the agentic web is where the boring daily admin of our lives happens. For instance, Krystian Kolondra, an executive vice president at the browser company Opera, doesn’t intend to use agents for every part of travel planning, even though this is often touted as one of their central use cases. “I don’t want to get an itinerary [from an AI] who has planned me every minute for something that was supposed to be fun,” he says. “I actually prefer to sit down with my wife in the evening and then just think [about] where to go next, what to see, and then enjoy that experience.”

He’s happy to fully relinquish some of the more routine parts of travel planning to agents, though: “Finding what the options are for flights? Why not?”

Mollick, however, thinks that the human web could be at risk. “If agents take over the web, then the web will change,” he says. “Do we abandon the human internet entirely and move to a world of private Discords? Do we strip down all the information so the AIs are just talking to each other rather than having an intermediary of a website to go through?”

“We have no idea,” he says. “We’re in this very early, weird stage of the evolution.”

articles.title: HK rises as mainland markets rebound on policy talk
articles.excerpt: The mainland's stock market rebounded on Monday after reports said regulators were preparing fresh support measures. In Hong Kong, the…
articles.fullText:
The mainland's stock market rebounded on Monday after reports said regulators were preparing fresh support measures.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended up close to 99 points, or 0.42 percent, at 23,393 on turnover of HK$204.84 billion.

The tech index surged 84 points, or 2.25 percent, to 3,839 while the China Enterprises Index rose 23 points, or 0.56 percent, to 7,906.

On the mainland, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended up 39 points, or 1.08 percent, at 3,638 on turnover of 847.46 billion yuan.

The blue-chip CSI300 Index ended 0.8 percent higher, recovering some ground following an 8.5 percent slump in October, its worst monthly performance in more than a decade as a selloff in technology stocks weighed on sentiment.

The Shenzhen Component Index rose 176 points, or 1.63 percent, to 11,010 on turnover of 936.23 billion yuan while the ChiNext surged 45 points, or 1.87 percent, to 2,458 on turnover of 466.78 billion yuan.

The rally came after media reports that the nation's central bank and securities watchdog would meet brokerages and fund managers on Monday to discuss measures to support capital markets and encourage lending for share buybacks and stock purchases.

Gains were also supported by a surge in trading volumes in exchange-traded funds favoured by the "National Team" of state-backed investors, fuelling speculation of official market support.

Meanwhile, the yuan hit a new more-than-four-year high against the dollar, as investors turned their attention to this week's US midterm elections for their possible impact on global financial markets.

The nation's central bank injected cash into the banking system, as it formally shifted its main policy rate to an overnight lending rate, a move analysts said would ease funding conditions and support the economy.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei share average ended 208 points, or 0.33 percent, lower at 63,081 as memory chipmaker Kioxia tanked and gains by Tokyo Electron and other firms with strong outlooks limited the losses. The broader Topix fell 34 points, or 0.88 percent, to 3,930.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed up 128 points, or 2.24 percent, at 5,859 as strong exports fuelled dip-buying sentiment in the chip sector. (Reuters & Xinhua)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: 30pc of financial firms now employ agentic AI: survey
articles.excerpt: The Securities and Futures Commission has released its first-ever AI readiness survey, showing that most large financial firms in Hong…
articles.fullText:
The Securities and Futures Commission has released its first-ever AI readiness survey, showing that most large financial firms in Hong Kong already use artificial intelligence across their operations, with adoption expected to accelerate over the coming year.

The survey, conducted between July and August this year, covered 20 large financial firms with 78 affiliated licensed corporations in Hong Kong. Together they accounted for over 75 percent of securities transactions reported by licensed corporations in the six months ended June.

The survey found that 95 percent of surveyed firms expected AI usage to accelerate over the next 12 months, with 90 percent already connecting AI tools to internal systems. AI use now spans front-, middle- and back-office activities.

"AI adoption in Hong Kong in the capital market is growing rapidly in speed and in scale," SFC chief executive officer Julia Leung said during the Hong Kong Fintech Week.

Notably, agentic AI – which can autonomously determine and execute steps to achieve an objective – is gaining traction, the survey showed.

Thirty percent of surveyed firms already use it in their business operations, and 25 percent are piloting it with varying degrees of autonomy and human involvement.

However, Leung struck a note of caution.

"Just think of agentic AI [as] your kids at home. They define the boundaries we set for them. They can go rogue, they can collude with their siblings, and disrupt your neighbour," she said.

Leung also acknowledged that the development of frontier AI models and agents has outpaced governments' and regulators' ability to set rules.

The SFC said the findings will inform its supervisory approach to AI, with priorities including protecting investors, strengthening cybersecurity and operational resilience, and ensuring effective AI governance.

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: NPC set to lay down law on cross-border corruption
articles.excerpt: The National People's Congress has begun deliberating on a draft law on combating cross-border corruption, including a provision on promoting…
articles.fullText:
The National People's Congress has begun deliberating on a draft law on combating cross-border corruption, including a provision on promoting the building of a fair and equitable global anti-corruption governance system.

The draft was submitted for its second reading at an NPC Standing Committee session that runs through Friday.

It further elaborates on the legislative purpose and enriches the principles guiding efforts to combat cross-border corruption.

It also stipulates that such efforts must be conducted in strict accordance with the Constitution and laws, follow statutory procedures, and respect and protect human rights.

The draft law was first submitted for deliberation in late August. The formulation of the law is an important step by China to put in place a systematic and comprehensive foreign-related legal framework for anti-corruption, according to the NPC.

Structured into six chapters and 47 articles, the draft sets out the principles, scope and key positions underpinning China's efforts to combat cross-border corruption.

The revised draft also sets out provisions on the use of information technology by authorities in combating cross-border corruption.

It requires relevant authorities and their staff to keep confidential any state secrets, work-related confidential information, trade secrets, personal privacy and personal information obtained during supervision and investigations.

It also requires Chinese companies operating across borders to set up integrity and compliance departments or appoint dedicated staff, based on their size, business scope, and risk prevention and control. (Xinhua)

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: HSBC to set up AI institute in race to train staff
articles.excerpt: Banking giant HSBC says an artificial intelligence and emerging technology institute being set up in Hong Kong is due to…
articles.fullText:
Banking giant HSBC says an artificial intelligence and emerging technology institute being set up in Hong Kong is due to become operational in the first quarter of 2027.

Announcing the update at Hong Kong Fintech Week on Monday, chief executive Georges Elhedery said the city's biggest lender aims to move the institute to the Northern Metropolis once a suitable location has been identified.

For now, he said the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology will be the institute’s first anchor academic partner.

"We bring their skills and know-how and capabilities as well as our domain expertise and financial services to find and work on solutions that make our clients' lives much easier in the age of AI, but also other emerging technologies such as blockchain, quantum, etc," Elhedery said.

He framed the institute's establishment as part of HSBC's broader AI strategy to give its roughly 200,000 employees – including about 28,000 in Hong Kong – an efficiency boost.

"AI is going to be disruptive. It’s going to transform jobs. It’s going to eliminate some. It’s going to create new ones," Elhedery said.

"The first mission for us is to bring all our colleagues … on the journey with us as opposed to creating an environment where uncertainty actually prevails."

HSBC is already testing how client agents could interact with the bank’s agents to handle basic tasks, he said, though security remains a major workstream.

On AI security, Elhedery said, HSBC is constantly working to identify vulnerabilities and build more resilient systems.

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: Armed police to patrol Sydney in wake of Bondi attack
articles.excerpt: A new police unit armed with military assault rifles has begun patrolling the streets of Sydney in an Australian-first measure…
articles.fullText:
A new police unit armed with military assault rifles has begun patrolling the streets of Sydney in an Australian-first measure set up in response to the Bondi Beach attack in December.

The Armed Response Command will deploy at major events, crowded public spaces, sporting venues and places of worship to conduct "high-visibility" patrols, New South Wales state police said.

The move comes after two men opened fire on a Jewish celebration at the famous beach, killing 15 people in an antisemitic attack motivated by Islamic State ideology.

The A$94 million unit is composed of 250 officers armed with Australian combat assault rifles.

The measure is the first of its kind in Australia, where the presence of heavily armed police officers is rare.

"The tragic events at Bondi demonstrated the devastating consequences when an alleged armed offender attacks innocent people," unit commander Detective Superintendent Andrew Evans said.

"The Armed Response Command ensures we have highly trained officers in the right places, with the right equipment, ready to act when seconds matter."

Amnesty International Australia said the introduction of heavily armed police patrols in Sydney raised "serious questions" about the increasing militarisation of policing and the safeguards in place to protect human rights. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HKMA eyes next level for Fintech 2030 with AI push
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has set out the next phase of its Fintech 2030 strategy, which will pair new…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has set out the next phase of its Fintech 2030 strategy, which will pair new technology initiatives with a renewed emphasis on governance and risk management.

Speaking at Hong Kong Fintech Week on Monday, authority chief executive Eddie Yue said the HKMA is launching Project Sage to examine the application and governance of "agentic finance" – artificial intelligence systems that can execute tasks on behalf of users.

"The main purpose of the Sage project is to hope that, under agentic finance, we can both promote application and pay attention to governance," he said.

Yue said a cross-sector expert panel would bring together finance, payments, professional services, technology and academic representatives to explore use cases, sandbox testing, interoperability standards and governance safeguards.

The HKMA is also issuing a discussion paper on banks’ use of agentic AI, seeking views on governance models, responsibility arrangements and a possible central register of trusted agents.

Yue said the aim is to set rules that allow innovation while managing risks.

He also said the authority would launch a post-quantum cryptography toolbox with the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology to help banks prepare for the challenges stemming from breakthroughs in quantum computing.

On tokenisation, Yue said the HKMA is introducing tokenised central bank money to enable 24/7 settlement of interbank tokenised deposits and would expand the number of participating banks to support cross-lender transfers around the clock.

"The benefit is that, for example, quite a number of enterprises with global liquidity to manage can, if round-the-clock tokenised deposit transfers are achieved, make payments at any time and anywhere, across different accounts and even cross-border," he said.

"And for retail investors, if in the future they want to invest in different retail tokenised financial products, they can also more flexibly do their investments 24/7, strengthening the flexibility and security of their asset allocation."

Yue said the HKMA would further pilot tokenised Exchange Fund Bills in the secondary market and explore whether regulated stablecoins could serve as a payment channel.

He stressed that innovation must be matched by governance and risk management so it can go further, land better and benefit more people.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: John Lee says HK offers businesses long-term certainty
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee said Hong Kong offers businesses the "certainty" they need to innovate, invest and flourish over the…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee said Hong Kong offers businesses the "certainty" they need to innovate, invest and flourish over the long term, even as global uncertainty persists.

That assurance came in opening remarks that he made on the first day of the region's annual flagship finance and technology event, Hong Kong Fintech Week and StartmeupHK, on Monday.

The conference brings together some 1,000 government leaders and fintech, finance and technology professionals from more than 100 countries and economies, along with around 800 exhibitors and startups and more than 30 delegations from the mainland and abroad.

Lee framed the event against a fast-changing global backdrop, saying technology is advancing at a remarkable speed, with artificial intelligence transforming industries and forcing businesses worldwide to adjust to shifting market conditions and unprecedented technological changes.

"In such an ever-changing, all-encompassing environment, one quality is becoming even more valuable — I'm talking about certainty," he said.

"Certainty about direction, certainty about opportunities, certainty about where businesses can invest, innovate and flourish in the long term."

Lee pointed to Hong Kong’s first-ever five-year plan, saying the strategic blueprint reinforces the city’s status as an international financial, maritime and trade centre and aviation hub, while accelerating its development as an international innovation and technology centre and a hub for high-calibre talent.

He also cited Hong Kong’s ranking as the world’s freest economy, its more than 1,400 fintech companies and InvestHK’s support for more than 550 overseas and mainland companies in the first nine months of the year, generating about US$9 billion in foreign direct investment and some 11,100 jobs.

He also pointed to the Northern Metropolis as a long-term source of opportunity, saying the mega project would create an innovation "through-train" that connects talent and research with commercialisation, capital and global markets.

Lee expressed confidence that Hong Kong’s future would be one for everyone – in business, finance, technology and beyond.

"If you believe that technology will define the future, if you believe that Asia will continue to drive global economic growth, and if you believe in the transformation taking place across China, then you must believe in Hong Kong's pivotal place in making it happen," he said.

"After all, it's in Hong Kong that you access global capital while remaining close to one of the world's most dynamic engines of innovation and growth."

He added that Hong Kong is a place where ideas can move from research to commercialisation and then into global markets – an East-meets-West city built on multilateralism, free trade and mutual opportunity.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, mainland rise as tech fears weigh on Nikkei, Kospi
articles.excerpt: Asian share markets mostly slipped on Monday as worries about the sustainability of the AI investment boom loomed over the…
articles.fullText:
Asian share markets mostly slipped on Monday as worries about the sustainability of the AI investment boom loomed over the tech sector, while the high price of oil limited the safe-haven appeal of sovereign bonds.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up seven points, or 0.03 percent, at 23,301.

The tech index rose 20 points, or 0.55 percent, to 3,775 while the China enterprises index edged up 14 points, or 0.18 percent, to 7,876.

The Shanghai Composite Index opened 15 points, or 0.4 percent, higher at 3,614.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 63 points, or 0.59 percent, up at 10,897 while the ChiNext Index rose 25 points, or 1.05 percent, to 2,439.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 318 points, or 0.51 percent, lower at 62,972, moved up into positive territory before slipping again to be 215 points lower at one stage before lunch.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 92 points, or 1.62 percent, down at 5,637 before regaining ground to be 87 points higher at one stage before noon.

The mixed openings came as concerns about negative cash flow and the sheer scale of AI capex saw the cost of insuring against corporate defaults blow out last week, while gold hit a one-year low amid talk stressed investors were selling to raise money for margin calls.

An added wrinkle is the US midterms, with a win by Democrats in either or both houses may result in more political hurdles for data centres.

Adding to the air of unease were withdrawals from Binance as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange went back online on Sunday after hackers stole billions from the platform last week.

All of which raises the stakes for earnings this week with Apple, AMD and Palantir set to report in the wake of Intel's near 29 percent tumble on Friday.

Analysts at Goldman Sachs expect capex by hyperscalers to almost double to US$800 billion this year, and rise further to US$1.2 trillion in 2027.

At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth of nearly 30 percent in 2026, slowing to 18 percent next year.

"Earnings results have underscored the fundamental challenge facing equity investors – earnings growth is strong, but it is no longer accelerating," wrote Ben Snider, Goldman's chief US equity strategist, in a note.

"Similarly, Q3 results support our view that AI investment spending will continue to grow but that the growth rate of AI capex is peaking."

The recent retreat in equities provided a reprieve for safe-haven bonds, with investors wondering if a sustained selloff in the stock market could deter the Federal Reserve from hiking interest rates in December.

Futures still imply a 72 percent chance of a quarter-point rate rise, but now only have 55 basis points of total tightening priced in compared to more than 70 basis points a month ago. (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Democrat turns on party and backs Republican
articles.excerpt: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s former opponent in the US Senate primary, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials on Sunday by endorsing…
articles.fullText:
Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s former opponent in the US Senate primary, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials on Sunday by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers as Democratic tensions boiled over days before the election that could determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill.

Stevens endorsed Rogers after attending a Detroit church service with him.

The remarkable show of support for the US President Donald Trump-backed candidate in the tightly contested race comes after she was uninvited to a joint event the same day with El-Sayed, who defeated the congresswoman by a slim margin in the August primary.

“Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away," Stevens said in a video announcing the endorsement, which led her top aide to quit.

“And he's right. And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.”

El-Sayed dismissed the endorsement when asked about it by reporters later Sunday, saying he's focused on issues voters care about, such as the high cost of living.

“At the end of the day I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens," he said, adding later: “None of this matters."

Michigan Democratic leaders were left shocked.

With less than 48 hours to go before Election Day, a party that had spent months trying to unite behind its Senate nominee was suddenly grappling with an extraordinary defection in one of this year's most important races.

Tensions between the two Democrats have festered since the primary.

Stevens is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a fierce critic of the US ally.

He has also been criticised by some in the community for past remarks regarding a Michigan synagogue attack and for appearances with controversial streamer Hasan Piker.

El-Sayed, a former Michigan public health official, is facing Rogers, an ex-congressman, for the seat held by the retiring Democrat, Gary Peters.

Keeping Michigan in Democratic hands is vital to the party’s effort to win a majority for the final two years of Trump’s second term. (AP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Nine killed in small plane crash in southern Florida
articles.excerpt: Nine people were killed on Sunday when the Learjet they were travelling in plummeted into a neighbourhood in southern Florida…
articles.fullText:
Nine people were killed on Sunday when the Learjet they were travelling in plummeted into a neighbourhood in southern Florida, just miles from US President Donald Trump's resort home of Mar-a-Lago, officials said.

Several unverified clips depicting the deadly crash and posted to social media show an aircraft nearly vertical slamming at high speed into the ground and triggering a large fireball, leaving a flaming crater near a busy roadside.

"Today's plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida is a horrific tragedy," US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement, confirming that all nine people on board were killed.

Duffy said the plane, a Learjet 60, had departed from Austin, Texas and was headed for the Bahamas.

The crash occurred near Cresthaven, a neighbourhood in Palm Beach County that is less than seven miles (11 kilometres) from Mar-a-Lago.

Trump himself had been at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday and had departed from the nearby and newly renamed President Donald J Trump International Airport shortly after he boarded Air Force One at 11.55am, about an hour before the crash of the Learjet aircraft.

Storms had been reported in the area, and Trump carried an umbrella as he boarded Air Force One.

"The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate," the crash, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Alcaraz crushes De Minaur for Vienna Open title
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz completed an unbeaten season in ATP 500-level events when he cruised past Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz completed an unbeaten season in ATP 500-level events when he cruised past Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in the Vienna Open final on Sunday.

Alcaraz closed out the victory on his first match point on De Minaur's serve, in one hour and 27 minutes to beat the Australian for the seventh time in as many meetings.

De Minaur battled hard.

He took seven games in the first set to deuce, but only won one.

In the second set, De Minaur, who entered the final on a 10-match indoor unbeaten streak, saved break points in three of his first four service games. Alcaraz forced the break he needed in the 10th and final game.

"His style is really dangerous," said Alcaraz.

"He's really fast, so you have to earn every point. You might hit a winner against everybody, except him. I had to be really focused on that."

"I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better, more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me."

Alcaraz did not drop a single set in five matches in Vienna as he claimed the 28th title of his career.

The victory followed his title in Tokyo four weeks ago.

Alcaraz also won in Doha in February before he was sidelined for almost five months with a wrist injury.

All three 500 titles came on hard courts.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion made his return to the courts at the US Open in New York, where he was eliminated in the quarterfinals.

Alcaraz said his form in Vienna had been encouraging.

"Obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me. I learned a lot, to keep going forward, step by step, playing on indoor courts, and trying to gain more confidence playing on this surface," he said. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Antonelli becomes youngest F1 world champion
articles.excerpt: Kimi Antonelli drove the perfect race to finish third in his Mercedes at the Mexico Grand Prix and seal his…
articles.fullText:
Kimi Antonelli drove the perfect race to finish third in his Mercedes at the Mexico Grand Prix and seal his place in Formula One history as the youngest world champion.

Max Verstappen took the chequered flag, but all eyes were on the young Italian who takes the crown at the age of 20 years and 68 days, more than three years younger than Sebastian Vettel in 2010.

He is the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

"We did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family," said an emotional Antonelli who has won nine races so far this season.

"I am very grateful for this moment, it will be with me forever. I am speechless, just trying to process what happened.

"It's been an incredible season and to share this podium with Max and Lewis (Hamilton) is incredible. I am looking forward to some more battles in the future."

The race broke into two parts as it was suspended after 46 of the 71 laps following a crash involving Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas.

The Finn's suspension on the front left side had collapsed causing his wheel to buckle and making him a helpless passenger as his car flew backwards off the track and slammed into the barriers.

The 37-year-old Bottas was slow to emerge from his car but waved to the crowd as he walked away, with all the other cars returning to the pits to await a restart.

Antonelli, who needed just to finish in the top nine to seal the title, was running third in his Mercedes when the race was stopped behind Red Bull's Verstappen and the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc.

His nearest challenger teammate George Russell was out of the running after suffering a poor start dropping from second on the grid to fifth and struggling with his power.

Russell had to win to have any hope of prolonging the title race.

Lewis Hamilton, who started on pole and also needed to win to push Antonelli, was furious with his Ferrari teammate after an incident at the start that saw Leclerc leave the track and steal the lead.

The Monegasque was handed a five-second penalty, but he retained track superiority over Hamilton.

That changed on the restart when Hamilton powered past Antonelli and Leclerc and bumped wheels with Verstappen before settling into second.

There was a further yellow flag when the Racing Bull of Arvid Lindblad also crashed out 10 laps from the end after tangling with the McLaren of Oscar Piastri.

Antonelli sat tight in third as Hamilton continued to press Verstappen.

It was entirely appropriate that the young Italian, in tears as he crossed the line, was led in by two of the all-time great drivers with 11 championships between them. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Houthi media issue fresh threats against Saudi targets
articles.excerpt: Houthi media, citing an anonymous military official, renewed threats on Sunday against Saudi oil giant Aramco and aviation in the…
articles.fullText:
Houthi media, citing an anonymous military official, renewed threats on Sunday against Saudi oil giant Aramco and aviation in the kingdom.

Yemen's Houthis, fighting a Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government, are allies of Iran, which on Sunday warned the US and Israel not to renew strikes on the Islamic republic after they had threatened a return to war.

"Aramco facilities are within range of the Yemeni Armed Forces, and investments in them are a venture fraught with losses," the Houthis' Saba news agency quoted the military official as saying.

The official also warned international airlines against using Saudi airspace "except for the airspaces of Mecca and Medina".

The Houthis have targeted oil facilities and airports in the kingdom since Yemen's once-dormant war reignited in July, killing 24 people in Saudi Arabia last month.

An October 10 strike on Riyadh's international airport became the deadliest on Saudi soil in years when it killed at least 13 people.

Meanwhile, fighting in Yemen has displaced more than 300,000 people in the western part of the impoverished country.

Most of them forced from their homes in the last two months, the displaced "urgently need shelter, food, clean water and health care", the International Organisation for Migration said in a statement on Sunday.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed since fighting in Yemen reignited.

Saba on Sunday said that Saudi Arabia had "targeted the Faculty of Medicine at Hodeidah University with two raids".

A fragile 2022 truce fell apart in July after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Swedish runner dominates at New York in first marathon
articles.excerpt: Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the New York City Marathon, clocking 2 hours 6 minutes 1 second in a spectacular debut…
articles.fullText:
Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the New York City Marathon, clocking 2 hours 6 minutes 1 second in a spectacular debut at the distance on Sunday.

The 31-year-old Almgren, in the spotlight after setting a European half-marathon record in Copenhagen last month, powered through the final mile to capture the victory over Italian Yemaneberhan Crippa, another runner better known for shorter distances.

Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race for a second time, repelling the challenge of last year's winner Hellen Obiri — who faded to finish third behind American Jessica McClain.

It is not the first time Chepkirui, who won in a time of 2hr 24.36, has dashed Obiri's dreams of successive wins.

In 2024 she edged then-defending champion Obiri on the streets of the Big Apple.

The race marked the 50th anniversary of the current incarnation of the NYC Marathon, which links the city's five boroughs of Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Manhattan.

The race was first run in 1970 when the course was confined to Central Park, the race becoming a city-wide event in 1976. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Canadian PM hints at improving relations with US
articles.excerpt: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday said he had a "good conversation" with US President Donald Trump on the…
articles.fullText:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday said he had a "good conversation" with US President Donald Trump on the two countries' fraying trade ties, after Washington imposed wide-ranging tariffs on its northern neighbour.

Carney said on social media that the latest talks built on "recent constructive discussions on the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal."

"Our teams will now be working in the coming weeks to deliver that outcome," he said.

In his second term, Trump has upended global trade by imposing tariffs on friends and foes alike, with Canada — one of the United States' biggest trading partners — often in his crosshairs.

High-level trade talks between the two countries broke down in August, prompting Trump to impose a host of new levies — some of which he has lifted ahead of crucial US midterm elections.

Affordability is a key issue for voters, and Trump's tariffs have fuelled inflation across the country.

The tariffs enforced after the August talks broke down impacted around US$20 billion worth of goods, ranging from hockey sticks to cement.

In response, Canada imposed levies on an equivalent amount of American products, leading Trump to retaliate with another round of tariffs of as much as 50 percent on certain goods.

Trump last week said he expected a new trade agreement with Canada to be reached "pretty soon," but offered no details.

The US president's chaotic trade policies have seen Canada deepen its engagement with other allies.

On Friday, the European Union and Canada announced an alliance that would see Ottawa become the bloc's first "associate member," although there was some disagreement within the EU over the use of that term. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Arsenal back in top spot after beating Liverpool 1-0
articles.excerpt: Champions Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League with Kai Havertz's early goal securing a…
articles.fullText:
Champions Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League with Kai Havertz's early goal securing a statement 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

German striker Havertz tapped in from Declan Rice's low cross in the 16th minute after the hosts were caught out trying to play the ball out of defence.

Liverpool responded strongly as halftime approached with Florian Wirtz curling a free kick against the crossbar and Alexis Mac Allister heading a good chance over the bar.

Arsenal weathered the storm, and defended superbly to keep Liverpool at arm's length after the break and seal their first Premier League win at Anfield for 14 years.

Mikel Arteta's side replace Manchester City at the top with 24 points from nine games, with City on 21 after losing at home to Brighton and Hove Albion on Saturday.

Liverpool's second league defeat of the season left them nine points behind Arsenal in fifth place. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: CE to visit Beijing, Shanghai
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee will depart for Beijing and Shanghai tomorrow to attend the 29th Beijing-Hong Kong Economic Cooperation Symposium…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee will depart for Beijing and Shanghai tomorrow to attend the 29th Beijing-Hong Kong Economic Cooperation Symposium and the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE).

Mr Lee said that Hong Kong will continue to deepen exchanges and co-operation with the Mainland. By participating in the events, the city aims to leverage its unique role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" under the "one country, two systems" principle.

He added that Hong Kong will further consolidate its position as a two-way platform to help Mainland enterprises expand globally while attracting foreign investment. This collaborative approach seeks to explore new economic opportunities for all parties.

Mr Lee will meet Beijing officials during his stay in the city and deliver a speech at the symposium’s opening ceremony on Wednesday.

Themed "Beijing-Hong Kong Together into the 15th Five Year Plan", this year's symposium focuses on driving deeper practical co-operation. It aims to harness complementary advantages to seize growth opportunities arising from the National 15th Five-Year Plan.

Mr Lee will depart for Shanghai later on Wednesday. He will attend the opening ceremony of the ninth CIIE and the Hongqiao International Economic Forum on Thursday.

The Chief Executive is scheduled to visit the Hong Kong exhibition area and address a sub-forum at the event. He will also hold meetings with Shanghai officials to further strengthen Shanghai-Hong Kong co-operation.

Mr Lee will return to Hong Kong on Friday. Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki will serve as Acting Chief Executive during his absence.

articles.title: New Wah Fu Estate plan briefed
articles.excerpt: The Housing Authority today briefed the Southern District Council on the latest progress of the clearance and rehousing plan for…
articles.fullText:
The Housing Authority today briefed the Southern District Council on the latest progress of the clearance and rehousing plan for the redevelopment of Wah Fu Estate (WFE) and consulted members on the proposed public housing development at New Wah Fu Estate (NWFE) Phase 1. The proposal has received general support.

Construction works for the proposed public housing developments in the five reception sites in Pok Fu Lam South are proceeding in an orderly manner, with the first reception estate, Wah Fu North Estate (WFNE) on Wah King Street, anticipated to be completed by late this year when residents of Wah On House and Wah Lok House will move in progressively.

The entire rehousing process is expected to conclude in the third quarter of 2027, after which demolition works will commence to clear the site for the construction of NWFE Phase 1 to meet the rehousing needs of the residents from Wah Chui House and Wah King House six years earlier.

To make effective use of public housing resources and provide diversified rehousing arrangements that meet the needs of residents affected by the clearance for the redevelopment of WFE Phase 1b, those living in Wah Cheong House, Wah Kin House and Wah Tai House who wish to transfer early to the newly completed public rental housing, the authority will launch a thinning-out exercise for these residents by offering more than 400 flats in WFNE for eligible residents' selection. Those who successfully select a flat are expected to complete the intake formalities in March next year.

The remaining four reception estates are also scheduled for completion successively between 2028 and 2031. Certain signature public spaces in the existing WFE will be recreated within the reception estates as highlights of the community.

NWFE adopted a community-oriented approach as its core design concept. Through the public engagement initiative, the design team has systematically fostered local consensus.

Additionally, the authority will continue to co-ordinate with the Highways Department's Railway Development Office and the MTR Corporation for the alignment of the South Island Line (West), the location of Wah Fu Station and the overall development planning. The master planning and design proposal for NWFE is expected to be substantially completed by the first half of 2028, and the HA will then submit a comprehensive proposal to the District Council.

“Rebuilding Wah Fu” is the design concept of NWFE Phase 1, involving the preservation and revitalisation of the existing Wah Fu (I) Shopping Centre and the “Banyan Tree Area” outside the shopping centre.

To create a larger parcel of land for the development of NWFE Phase 1, a section of the existing Wah Fu Road will be realigned. The authority will arrange gazettal of the relevant road works in early 2027 and will commence the relevant works in mid-2028.

The pedestrian facilities and road improvement works being carried out in the Pok Fu Lam South area by the Civil Engineering & Development Department are expected to be completed by 2027.Meanwhile, the MTR Corporation is currently conducting detailed planning and design for the South Island Line (West) with the project expected to be completed and in operation by 2034 or earlier.

articles.title: CE meets education minister
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee today met Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng to exchange views on deepening co-operation and exchanges. Welcoming…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee today met Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng to exchange views on deepening co-operation and exchanges.

Welcoming Mr Huai to Hong Kong, Mr Lee noted that the city is home to five of the world’s top 100 universities, with its education competitiveness ranking among the highest globally.

He said the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is fully implementing the First Five-Year Plan to develop the city into an international hub for high-calibre talent. Through the Task Force on Study in Hong Kong, the city actively attracts outstanding global students.

Mr Lee highlighted that the inaugural Study in Hong Kong Week was launched this year. The Asia-Pacific Association for International Education 2026 Conference, held as part of the event, was the largest ever, underscoring the international influence of Hong Kong's post-secondary education.

Leveraging its unique advantages under the “one country, two systems” principle, Hong Kong will roll out the “Hong Kong: Your World-class Campus” international publicity campaign and support local institutions in recruiting students from the Mainland and overseas.

Furthermore, Mr Lee outlined the accelerated development of the Northern Metropolis (NM), which will feature a university town as its core focus to integrate education, technology, industry, talent and urban development. This integration will create a strategic platform for high-level post-secondary education, innovation and technology synergy, and high-end talent clustering.

The Chief Executive added that the Hong Kong SAR Government will strengthen co-operation with the Ministry of Education to encourage more top-tier Mainland higher education and research institutions to establish a presence in the NM. This move aims to pool top academic strengths, promote the commercialisation of research outcomes, and achieve mutual benefits.

Regarding regional integration, Mr Lee pointed out that higher education co-operation within the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) is thriving. Currently, all eight University Grants Committee-funded universities have established industry-education-research bases in Shenzhen, while four have set up campuses in Mainland GBA cities.

Coinciding with the 10th anniversary of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao University Alliance this year, the Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to enhance collaboration mechanisms between local and Mainland education institutions.

Mr Lee expressed confidence that both sides would further deepen collaboration in teacher training, digital education and patriotic education, jointly contributing to the country's development as a leading nation in education.

Also attending the meeting were Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin and Director of the Chief Executive's Office Carol Yip.

articles.title: HK welcomes UNIDROIT office launch
articles.excerpt: Professor Enzo Moavero-Milanesi, (President of the International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT)), Professor Ignacio Tirado (Secretary-General of…
articles.fullText:
Professor Enzo Moavero-Milanesi, (President of the International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT)), Professor Ignacio Tirado (Secretary-General of the UNIDROIT), Commissioner Cui Jianchun (Commissioner of the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

Good morning, and welcome to Hong Kong.

It is my honour and privilege to be here, with you, at the opening of the UNIDROIT Centenary Regional Conference for the Asia-Pacific.

This is a day of double celebration. Today we commemorate 100 years of UNIDROIT's extraordinary contribution to the modernisation and harmonisation of private law. Equally significant, we are here to witness the opening of a new chapter of UNIDROIT – the establishment of its inaugural office outside its seat in Rome, right here in Asia's World City, Hong Kong.

UNIDROIT was established in 1926, under the auspices of the League of Nations. Back then, few could have imagined the profound impact it would have on the global legal landscape in the century to follow.

Today, UNIDROIT stands as one of the world's oldest international organisations dedicated to strengthening the rule of law in international private and commercial law. Its 65 member states come from five continents.

While the League of Nations no longer exists, UNIDROIT remains a prominent and independent inter-governmental organisation based on the 1940 UNIDROIT Statute.

Its mission – to study the needs and methods for modernising, harmonising and co-ordinating private and commercial law among states, formulating uniform law instruments, principles and rules to achieve those objectives – has become more relevant than ever.

UNIDROIT has been instrumental in reducing legal barriers to trade, investment and cross-border co-operation. In doing so, it promotes the connectivity and prosperity that our region treasures.

So, yes, Hong Kong gladly welcomes the establishment of the UNIDROIT Asia-Pacific Liaison Office in our city.

It is a decision of profound significance – for UNIDROIT, for Hong Kong and for the entire Asia-Pacific region.

The liaison office will serve as a focal point for enhanced engagement with member states and stakeholders in the region. And it will play a crucial role in the legislative and institutional work of UNIDROIT.

Hong Kong, strategically located at the heart of Asia, is an ideal home for the Asia-Pacific liaison office.

We are a renowned international legal, trade and financial hub, and a host to many international organisations.

Hong Kong is also the only common law jurisdiction within China, our country, operating under the unique principle of "one country, two systems". Our legal system is renowned for its robust rule of law, buttressed by a deep pool of legal talent.

Our laws and dispute resolution framework are well aligned with international standards and recognised globally. Indeed, the 2026 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index, published last month, ranks Hong Kong sixth in East Asia and the Pacific, and within the first quintile out of 143 countries and jurisdictions.

And Hong Kong maintained its position within the top 10 globally in "Absence of Corruption" and "Order and Security".

The National 15th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong in deepening its development as an international legal and dispute resolution services centre. Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, launched in September, sets out a range of measures to harness the unique advantages of our common law system.

And this year's Policy Address reaffirms our commitments in greater detail, specifically noting our support for the establishment of the UNIDROIT Asia-Pacific Liaison Office in Hong Kong.

The liaison office will also enjoy benefits from co-operation with other partner organisations here. That includes the International Organization for Mediation, headquartered in Hong Kong since last year, as well as the Asian-African Legal Consultative Organization's Hong Kong Regional Arbitration Centre and the Hague Conference on Private International Law's Regional Office for the Asia-Pacific.

The liaison office may also enjoy benefits from the stakeholder network established by the Hong Kong International Legal Talents Training Academy. The Academy was launched by the Department of Justice two years ago this month.

Working together, I'm confident the two organisations can address UNIDROIT's needs for capacity building. Such legal co-operation is essential in a city that thrives on openness, connectivity and rules-based international order.

We strive to attract global organisations and talent, enable international legal co-operation and position Hong Kong as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" for East and West. The Asia-Pacific accounts for more than 40 per cent of global GDP and encompasses vital trade corridors.

The liaison office reflects the importance of the Asia-Pacific region in UNIDROIT's work and will deepen collaboration, resulting in a better understanding and implementation of private law. This liaison office is a symbol of our collective ambition to build a more harmonious and prosperous future for the Asia-Pacific and beyond.

I wish to thank UNIDROIT for its enduring trust in Hong Kong, and to express my gratitude to our country for its staunch and unwavering support, without which this milestone would not have been possible. My thanks, as well, to all of you for your commitment to this shared endeavour.

I am confident that the establishment of the liaison office will strengthen the long-standing collaborative relationship between Hong Kong and UNIDROIT, serving as a catalyst for deeper engagement throughout the region. Let us continue to work together – to harmonise, connect and build a future rooted in peace and prosperity.

I wish this conference and the liaison office every success. The conference, let me add, is the opening event of this year's Hong Kong Legal Week, five days of high-profile discussions and gatherings designed to strengthen regional and cross-sector collaboration, including the Second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum and the third Asia-Pacific International Private Law Summit.

For those of you here from overseas, I wish you a memorable stay in Hong Kong, the world's rising East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchange, and legal exchange, too.

Chief Executive John Lee gave this speech at Hong Kong Legal Week 2026: UNIDROIT Centenary: Regional Conference for the Asia-Pacific and Opening Ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Liaison Office on November 2.

articles.title: Legal Week kicks off
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, themed “Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future” began today. An annual flagship…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, themed “Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future” began today.

An annual flagship event for the legal sector organised by the Department of Justice (DoJ) Legal Week 2026 brings together legal professionals, business leaders, policymakers, academics and leading international legal organisations from Hong Kong and around the world to have in-depth discussions and exchanges on forward-looking issues such as regional legal co-operation, international dispute resolution and lawtech.

Marking the centenary celebration of the International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT) and the 60th anniversary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), both leading international legal organisations will hold celebratory events during Legal Week, making this year's programme particularly significant.

UNIDROIT Centenary: Regional Conference for Asia-Pacific and Opening Ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Liaison Office was held as the opening event of this year's Legal Week.

The opening ceremony was officiated by Chief Executive John Lee, Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Cui Jianchun, President of UNIDROIT Prof Enzo Moavero-Milanesi, Secretary-General of UNIDROIT Prof Ignacio Tirado and Secretary for Justice Paul Lam.

With the support of the central government, the DoJ has successfully secured the establishment of UNIDROIT's first office outside its seat in Rome in its 100 years of history, demonstrating Hong Kong's leading role as an international legal hub.

In his welcome remarks, Mr Lee said that today marks a double celebration, commemorating UNIDROIT's centenary and witnessing the opening of a new chapter for UNIDROIT – the establishment of its Asia-Pacific Liaison Office in Hong Kong. He noted that as a renowned international legal, trade and financial hub, Hong Kong strives to attract global organisations and talent, enable international legal co-operation and position Hong Kong as a super connector and super value-adder for East and West.

Mr Lee noted that by setting up a liaison office in Hong Kong, UNIDROIT not only enjoys benefits from co-operation with other partner organisations in the city, but also benefits from the network established by the Hong Kong International Legal Talents Training Academy to promote capacity building in the region. The establishment of the office is a symbol of the collective ambition to build a more harmonious and prosperous future for the Asia-Pacific and beyond.

Director-General of the Department of Treaty & Law, Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China Yu Ning said in her video speech that UNIDROIT setting up a liaison office in Hong Kong reflects the international community's high regard for Hong Kong and marks a significant achievement in the city's continuous effort in building itself as an international legal centre.

She said that in recent years, the Hong Kong SAR has continued to strengthen its exchanges and co-operation with UNIDROIT under the framework of “one country, two systems”, further showcasing to the world its strengths including its robust common law system, well-established judicial system and extensive pool of international legal talent.

Delivering his opening remarks, Mr Lam said that Hong Kong's relationship with UNIDROIT is longstanding. The establishment of the liaison office in Hong Kong will take the city's relationship with UNIDROIT to the next level, and will provide a stable and effective platform in the Asia-Pacific region to facilitate the development of international private law.

He noted that the presence of the three major private international law organisations at the Hong Kong legal hub, namely the UNIDROIT Asia-Pacific Liaison Office, the Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific of the Hague Conference on Private International Law, and the DoJ Project Office for Collaboration with United Nations Commission on International Trade Law, together with the International Organization for Mediation, the Asian African Legal Consultative Organization Hong Kong Regional Arbitration Centre and other international institutions, will create synergy.

The Regional Conference for the Asia-Pacific in celebration of UNIDROIT's centenary came right after the opening ceremony. More than 700 registrations from more than 40 countries or regions gathered to review UNIDROIT's achievements of a century in modernising and harmonising private law, and to explore how it can continue to foster regional development in its next century.

Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan said in his closing remarks that UNIDROIT opening its first ever overseas office in Hong Kong fully reflects the international community's vote of confidence in Hong Kong's legal system.

He pointed out that the Liaison Office will serve not only as a platform for dialogue with governments on the development and implementation of its instruments, but also as a hub for collaboration with academia, arbitral and mediation institutions, financial institutions and other key stakeholders.

The 3rd Asia-Pacific International Private Law Summit will be held tomorrow. Other events during Legal Week include the celebration event of UNCITRAL's 60th anniversary to be held on November 4, the Fourth Legal Forum on Interconnectivity and Development and the Hong Kong Mediation Lecture 2026 on November 5, as well as the Second Guangdong - Hong Kong - Macao Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum on November 6.

Additionally, the three-day Hong Kong LawTech Fest 2026 will begin on Wednesday.

Click here for details of the event.

articles.title: FinTech Week opens
articles.excerpt: The 11th edition of the five-day Hong Kong FinTech Week kicked off today at the Convention & Exhibition Centre in…
articles.fullText:
The 11th edition of the five-day Hong Kong FinTech Week kicked off today at the Convention & Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai, drawing over 1,000 government and business leaders and around 800 exhibitors and startups.

Opening the event, Chief Executive John Lee highlighted the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government’s inaugural Five-Year Plan, underscoring the city’s role as a multi-hub powerhouse and driving regional synergy with Shenzhen and the wider Greater Bay Area through the Northern Metropolis serving as a new “South-North dual engine”.

Mr Lee said: “Less than two months ago, the Hong Kong SAR Government unveiled Hong Kong’s first-ever Five-Year Plan for Economic & Social Development. It is closely aligned with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, which sets out a clear direction for Hong Kong to leverage its strengths and better integrate into, and serve, the overall national development.”

“Our inaugural Five-Year Plan portrays Hong Kong’s outlook for businesses, investors and innovators, helping you capitalise on the far-reaching promise of Hong Kong – the abundance of opportunities arising from national and global development,” Mr Lee added.

Mainland enterprises turned out in force. The Shenzhen Fintech Association brought a delegation for the fourth consecutive year, expanding its group to 20 companies, viewing Hong Kong as an ideal “super-connector” and a strategic springboard for global expansion.

Meanwhile, the Zhongguancun Fintech Industry Development Alliance highlighted Hong Kong’s capital market as a vital gateway for scaling Mainland tech firms onto the global stage.

The alliance’s Secretary-General added that the city leverages its rich concentration of financial institutions and international talent pool.

International delegations also seized the spotlight. A Malaysian delegation focused on artificial intelligence and virtual asset technologies, highlighting cross-gateway opportunities connecting the Association of Southeast Asian Nations markets.

“Hong Kong has always been the financial institution hub. Therefore, to penetrate China, I think it is best to penetrate Hong Kong first,” Malaysian delegation member Kay Moris said.

“We are looking at collaboration in terms of giving services to basically institutions in Hong Kong to penetrate into Southeast Asia and vice versa. So that we can also work as a collaborative partner to serve Hong Kong and China.”

Canada’s 20-firm delegation echoed a similar sentiment. Hong Kong Economic & Trade Office (Toronto) Head of Business & Talent Attraction/Investment Promotion Christopher Chen said: “We see Hong Kong as the trading port between Canada and China. Both countries have lots of resources that they want from each other. Invest Hong Kong plays a crucial role in introducing Canadian companies to China via the Hong Kong platform.”

Mr Chen also noted that prime geography, top-tier talent, and massive assets under management solidify Hong Kong’s unmatched standing across Asia.

articles.title: Party releases resolution after plenum on governance
articles.excerpt: The Communist Party of China (CPC) on Sunday made public a resolution following this week's annual plenary session in Beijing…
articles.fullText:
The Communist Party of China (CPC) on Sunday made public a resolution following this week's annual plenary session in Beijing.

The document titled "The Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance", was released by Xinhua News Agency.

In an explanation of the resolution also published by Xinhua, President Xi Jinping explained that Party building is crucial for the future of the CPC.

Xi acknowledged that the makeup of the Party has changed.

"Over the years, our Party membership is undergoing structural changes, with a steady increase in the proportion of members and officials born after the launch of reform and opening up in 1978. This has raised new requirements for education and management," he said.

"The vast majority of Party members are exemplary, yet there remain a number of problems and hidden dangers that threaten to undermine the Party’s advanced nature, weaken its integrity, and jeopardise its long-term governance.

"In particular, the problems of defects in thinking, organisation, and conduct have yet to be solved root and branch, while some new problems continue to emerge," he explained.

The resolution itself called for stricter monitoring of officials.

"Starting with high-ranking officials, we will tighten all-around management and regular oversight of officials, imposing strict requirements throughout their career and across the whole process of their education, management, and oversight to avoid over-emphasising selection to the neglect of management," it said.

"The system requiring leading officials to report personal information will be refined.

"Those with family property and spending far exceeding their normal incomes will be examined, and relevant verifications will be carried out. Regular management will be tightened for the commercial and entrepreneurial activities of leading officials’ spouses, children, and their children’s spouses. Dedicated efforts will be intensified to address nepotism," it wrote.

Xi in the explanation also said that the nation’s success hinges on the CPC, "especially on the Party’s efforts to exercise full and rigorous self-governance".

"In the face of complicated international and domestic landscapes and the challenging tasks of advancing reform, promoting development, and ensuring stability, it is essential, in our efforts to ensure steady and sustained progress in Chinese modernisation," Xi said.

The fifth plenum, which ended on Thursday, comes ahead of a major Party congress next year, where Xi is expected to oversee a leadership reshuffle.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: UAE says hoping for breakthrough in Iran-US war
