articles.excerpt: The United Arab Emirates is hoping for a breakthrough in negotiations between Iran and the United States while being prepared…
articles.fullText:
The United Arab Emirates is hoping for a breakthrough in negotiations between Iran and the United States while being prepared for the worst, a senior official said on Sunday, following threats of a resumption of the Middle East war.

"We're hoping that there is a diplomatic breakthrough," diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president Anwar Gargash said during a conference in Manama.

"It is not the interest of the region to go through another round... But I think we're also, as we've shown before, braced for the worst."

Following a visit to Tehran this week by a Qatari delegation, Iran has dispatched envoys to the Gulf country to continue consultations as part of indirect negotiations with the US to end the war.

But US President Donald Trump reiterated his threats on Saturday, saying the United States still has to "take care of" one or two targets in Iran.

"We just can't allow Iran to take this region and the global economy hostage," US Assistant Secretary for Near Eastern Affairs Donald Blome said at the Manama conference on Sunday.

"The hand of negotiation has been extended, and those channels have continued to be open and active at the same time," Blome said. "We've been also prepared to go in another direction."

On Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran and that the US would be open to a diplomatic solution.

The war began on February 28 with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: France probes petrol-bomb attack on police
articles.excerpt: France has launched an attempted murder investigation after a petrol bomb was thrown at security forces during a weekend protest…
articles.fullText:
France has launched an attempted murder investigation after a petrol bomb was thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors said on Sunday.

On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and some other cities after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs.

The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail.

"Explosive devices were thrown at around fifteen gendarmes as well as police officers," the prosecutor's office said on Sunday.

Gendarmes are military police officers who are part of the French armed forces.

Prosecutors said an investigation had been opened for "attempted murder of persons vested with public authority".

Dramatic images showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in eastern Paris.

An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding the reported injuries include second-degree burns.

No suspects "have been arrested at this stage in connection with the incident," the prosecutor's office said, adding that investigators were working to identify those responsible.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez on Saturday decried an "extraordinary" level of violence from some rioters. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Evacuees from occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine
articles.excerpt: Residents of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ravaged by years of war, arrived in Ukraine on Saturday after being evacuated…
articles.fullText:
Residents of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ravaged by years of war, arrived in Ukraine on Saturday after being evacuated via Belarus during a rare truce brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.

An AFP journalist saw the residents, some draped in Ukrainian flags, disembark buses and tearfully embrace their loved-ones in emotional scenes.

The city of Oleshky in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, occupied by the Russian military since 2022, had been caught in intense fighting between the two sides that had left residents unable to escape and starving.

Announcing the ceasefire last week, First Lady Melania Trump described the city as being "on the brink of disaster" and said that without her intervention, bringing aid to its beleaguered residents would have been "impossible".

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on X: "As of now, Ukrainian citizens from Oleshky have crossed the Ukrainian border."

"All of them will receive the assistance they need," he added.

Ukrainian and Russian officials visited the city together on Friday, delivering aid and marshalling those who wanted to leave in a rare show of cooperation between the warring sides.

The truce, which began early Tuesday, has marked the longest pause in fighting between Russia and Ukraine anywhere on the front line, and comes more than four-and-a-half years into a conflict that has left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead.

It is scheduled to end on Sunday evening.

In northern Ukraine, friends and relatives of those being evacuated had anxiously awaited their return.

Daryna Goncharova, 40, said earlier she was waiting to see her parents who were trapped in the town.

When asked what she would tell them when they arrived, she said: "That I love them."

Yelyzaveta Paliy, who was waiting for her father to return, said she never expected him to be gone so long.

"We last saw him at the end of January 2024, when my sister, mum and I left, and he stayed behind," the 19-year-old said.

"Sadly, two years have already passed, and so far, it's just been an evacuation," she said, expressing hope the city could return to Ukrainian control.

Captured by Russia in 2022, locals in the city had faced food, water and medicine shortages for months, while some were forced to hunt and eat pigeons, former residents told AFP.

Around 2,000 residents — compared with 24,000 before the war began — were still in Oleshky ahead of the humanitarian operation, according to Kyiv's estimates.

Neither Moscow nor Kyiv has specified the number of people evacuated, and authorities in both countries previously indicated that many residents wished to remain in the city, even in the event of renewed fighting.

Russia, which denies targeting civilians, now occupies around a fifth of its neighbour: the Crimean peninsula, which it annexed in 2014, most of the eastern regions of Donetsk and Lugansk — collectively referred to as the Donbas — and large parts of the southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions.

US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume in November, having been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, Russia fired more than 100 drones overnight, according to the Ukrainian air force.

The capital Kyiv was suffering electricity shortages again on Saturday, following Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure the day before, private Ukrainian energy provider DTEK said. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Brighton beat City; United implode against Chelsea
articles.excerpt: Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points…
articles.fullText:
Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday, while Manchester United slumped to another damaging defeat for Michael Carrick at Chelsea.

Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first ever away win against City at the 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title.

The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials.

Fabian Hurzeler's men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday.

Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead.

Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time.

But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side-netting late on.

City won their opening seven league games as Enzo Maresca made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola.

However, the 10-time English champions know their results on the field may count for little this season unless they can successfully overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.

City have appealed, but if that ruling is upheld they are likely to face a severe points penalty and possible relegation from the English top-flight.

Defeat for Maresca's men means Arsenal can go top of the table if they avoid losing at Liverpool on Sunday.

Manchester United's nine-game winless run is their longest without victory for 38 years after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

The Red Devils were left to regret not taking advantage of a series of first half chances to take the lead before they imploded in the second period.

Morgan Rogers was allowed to run straight through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring.

Lisandro Martinez then did his under-pressure manager no favours with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty.

Cole Palmer converted from the spot to lift Chelsea into the top four.

"The two halves of football couldn't probably be further apart," said Carrick, who added he expects to be in charge for Tuesday's Champions League tie against Roma.

"We looked in a good place going into half-time and then found a way of unravelling it second half."

Only Nottingham Forest's 2-0 defeat at Brentford ensured United did not drop into the bottom three.

Nikola Milenkovic's own goal and Igor Thiago's strike took the Bees up to sixth.

Bournemouth extended their fine form with a 2-0 win over Leeds thanks to goals from Evanilson and Amine Adli.

Sunderland remain rooted to the foot of the table after a 3-1 defeat at Coventry.

Hull and Ipswich played out a 2-2 draw. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Fernandez to face off against Shnaider in Tokyo final
articles.excerpt: Leylah Fernandez hailed her "mental fortitude" on Saturday after setting up a Pan Pacific Open title clash against Russia's Diana…
articles.fullText:
Leylah Fernandez hailed her "mental fortitude" on Saturday after setting up a Pan Pacific Open title clash against Russia's Diana Shnaider.

The World No. 23 from Canada defeated Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova 7-5, 6-3 in Tokyo to reach a second final in a row.

Fernandez won her first title of the season in Singapore in September and followed that up by reaching the decider last week in Ningbo, where she lost to world number one Elena Rybakina.

Fernandez will face 13th-ranked Shnaider after she beat Slovakian 18-year-old Mia Pohankova 6-4, 7-6 (9/7) in the other semi-final.

Fernandez put her success in this year's Asian swing down to a "willingness to work".

"I'm proud of my mental fortitude," said the 24-year-old, the US Open finalist in 2021.

"These aren't easy matches so I'm happy that I was able to find solutions and stay calm in tough moments."

Fernandez reached the semi-finals when Rybakina withdrew from their match with a neck injury, a day after securing the year-end world number one ranking.

Rybakina is one of several players who pulled out in Tokyo, which comes near the end of the tennis season.

Fernandez said she and her team decided to play as many matches as possible after the US Open in September, when she lost in the third round.

"We all agreed that what I needed the most was matches, to play in these tough matches, uncomfortable moments, and to be strong in those moments," she said.

"We could train all we want but we're not going to be able to replicate those difficult moments in training."

Shnaider is looking for her first title of the year after battling past former junior Wimbledon champion Pohankova.

"The work never stops," said Shnaider, 22, who beat Alexandra Eala in the quarter-finals.

"I had good preparation for the Asian swing from a fitness point of view.

"Yesterday was a very tough match and today I was happy that I managed to push myself again." (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Telling infrastructure stories well
articles.excerpt: Jointly launched by the Development Bureau and the Construction Industry Council, the “Hong Kong Infrastructure NO. 1” campaign seeks to…
articles.fullText:
Jointly launched by the Development Bureau and the Construction Industry Council, the “Hong Kong Infrastructure NO. 1” campaign seeks to deepen public understanding of the city’s infrastructure projects.

Through guided tours, interactive workshops, exhibitions and tailored teaching materials, the campaign shares professional engineering knowledge in an engaging and accessible way, allowing young people to explore careers in the construction industry.

Awe-inspiring visit
A group of primary school pupils toured the education centre at Plant Number 3 of the Kai Tak District Cooling System, where they learnt about the climate challenges facing Hong Kong and how the cooling system works.

Interactive exhibits helped the pupils understand the technology behind the system, while a tour of the plant’s core facilities gave them a close-up view of its large-scale machinery and extensive network of pipes.

The facility completely defied the expectations of Primary 5 pupil Horace Tang.

“I was amazed by the sheer size of the plant and its enormous pipes,” he said.

“I think the district cooling system is remarkable because it helps reduce carbon emissions and save energy. The tour has inspired me to become an engineer in the future.”

Hands-on learning
The initiative focuses on three key areas: education, public engagement and media promotion.

On the education front, the campaign organises guided tours and engineering visits, while also providing a dedicated resource centre, interactive workshops and tailored learning and teaching materials.

The construction-themed materials integrate science, technology, engineering, the arts and mathematics, allowing students to explore subjects such as urban planning in an engaging and practical manner.

Moving beyond classroom concepts, students actively design their own communities within strict special limits and specific guidelines.

Secondary 3 pupil Chui Ki-hin said the workshop transformed his understanding of urban planning.

“I used to think urban planning was simple - that you could just arrange buildings like building blocks and connect the necessary utilities,” he said.

“However, after taking part in the workshop, I realised that it is much more complicated and that there are many constraints to consider.”

Even producing a small model required considerable thought and effort.

“It took me about 45 minutes just to complete this small model. I can only imagine how much more challenging it is to plan a real city.”

International recognition
Apart from its education initiatives, the campaign reaches the community through videos, social media content, exhibitions, quizzes and other public engagement activities.

The campaign’s impact has resonated far beyond Hong Kong. At the 23rd International Business Awards, the promotional initiative triumphed across 10 different categories - capturing six Gold and three Silver awards, as well as one Bronze.

“The aim is to use interesting and heartfelt stories to help the public more easily understand the advanced technologies adopted in infrastructure projects that we see in everyday life, and appreciate the craftsmanship spirit of our construction industry professionals,” Principal Assistant Secretary for Development (Works) Chris Ng said.

He added that Hong Kong’s global standing in engineering would not be possible without the commitment and expertise of industry professionals.

Construction Industry Council General Manager - Corporate Communications Hanks Lee said the trickiest part of the campaign was figuring out how to share professional engineering know-how in a down-to-earth and lively way.

“With the wholehearted support of the industry providing invaluable experience, practical examples and on-site assistance, we were able to tell the story of Hong Kong’s infrastructure.”

Looking ahead, the Development Bureau will continue to leverage digital and innovative media to showcase the technological advancement and professionalism of the construction industry. Through these efforts, it aims to deepen public understanding of the vital role infrastructure plays in Hong Kong’s economic, social and livelihood development, while attracting more young people to join the industry and carry forward the spirit of striving for excellence.

articles.title: Alibaba's Qwen and Apple Intelligence team up
articles.excerpt: Chinese tech giant Alibaba Group announced a partnership with Apple on Saturday to integrate its Qwen AI model into Apple…
articles.fullText:
Chinese tech giant Alibaba Group announced a partnership with Apple on Saturday to integrate its Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence.

The Qwen-powered feature will be available for testing in the latest iOS developer beta starting November 4, and roll out to Chinese users with the official iOS 27.3 release in December, according to Alibaba.

The partnership brings Qwen's AI capabilities to multiple use cases within Apple's operating system. Through Siri, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence, Chinese users will be able to tap Qwen's capabilities for text and image understanding and content generation.

Notably, users can choose whether to enable the Qwen integration and what information to share. Alibaba said it will not use user requests or generated responses for model training.

The feature will be available on iOS to users who purchase an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone in China, or whose device location and Apple Account country or region are both set to China.

Eddie Wu, CEO of Alibaba Group, said Qwen drawing on Alibaba's AI expertise will integrate into Apple's ecosystem and work with Apple to deliver new AI-powered service experiences to Chinese users.

Wang Xiaojie, an AI expert at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, said this is the first time a top global consumer hardware maker has used a Chinese large model as the primary system-level AI backbone in the Chinese market, a significant step in the commercial application of domestic large models.

Apple Intelligence is the AI system Apple first unveiled at its Worldwide Developers Conference in 2024. In a key regulatory move, China's cyberspace authority completed the filing of seven on-device generative AI services for smartphones in July, including Apple Intelligence. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Hakimi bags hat-trick as PSG rip Le Havre to pieces
articles.excerpt: Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom…
articles.fullText:
Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1.

PSG's nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice to drop four points adrift while Olivier Giroud's late goal lifted Lille second after their 1-0 home win over Lens.

The former World Cup and Champions League winner Giroud is now 40 and came off the bench to net his third goal of the season to settle a tense, tight struggle.

PSG have won six league games in a row after a slow start this term and top the table with 20 points. Lille are second on 18 but Monaco can join them should they beat Paris FC on Sunday, while Rennes have 16.

On just two points so far, Le Havre gave their opponents a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes.

Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi pass to level on 26 minutes.

Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1.

The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the 'keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up.

Senny Mayulu ran around Bodard, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net to effectively end the contest, just after the hour.

Hakimi completed his hat-trick when Bodard saved his initial effort, only for the ball to rebound off the Morocco international and loop into the net on 69 minutes. He had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off.

"He's a striker when we have the ball. He's free to do that when we are in possession, but obliged to defend when we aren't," said Luis Enrique.

The Spanish coach left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench, while Ousmane Dembele was absent through injury and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia faces the prospect of missing the rest of the season after tearing his ACL in last week's Champions League win over Barcelona. (AFP)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Chinese factory activity slips amid strong tech show
articles.excerpt: China's manufacturing activity moderated in October, with the purchasing managers' index falling to 49.3 as the high-tech and equipment manufacturing…
articles.fullText:
China's manufacturing activity moderated in October, with the purchasing managers' index falling to 49.3 as the high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors maintained expansion, official data showed on Saturday.

The overall reading was down 0.8 percentage points from September, according to the National Bureau of Statistics.

Chief statistician Huo Lihui attributed the retreat to some demand being brought forward ahead of the National Day holiday this month and a complex international environment.

The production subindex stood at 49.8, down 1.9 points from September, while the new-orders subindex fell 1.1 points to 49.4, as both supply and demand moderated during the month.

The PMI for high-tech manufacturing stood at 51.3 while that for equipment manufacturing came in at 50.6, both remaining above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction.

The figures indicate that emerging industries continued to sustain growth momentum, supported by the ongoing development of new quality productive forces, Huo noted.

Manufacturing activity in several advanced industries remained robust.

Both the production and new-orders subindexes for railway, shipbuilding and aerospace equipment manufacturing, as well as computer, communications and electronic equipment manufacturing, stood at 53 or above, pointing to relatively strong supply and demand in these sectors.

Large manufacturers continued to report expansion, with their PMI standing at 50.2, despite a slight decline of 0.4 points from the previous month.

The PMI readings for medium-sized and small enterprises came in at 48.4 and 47.5, respectively.

On the price front, both major raw material purchasing prices and factory-gate prices remained in expansionary territory, although their growth moderated.

The purchasing price subindex stood at 56.8, down four points from September while the factory-gate price subindex eased 2.3 points to 51.7, partly reflecting recent declines in the prices of certain nonferrous metals and other commodities. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Kane edges Mbappe by narrow margin
articles.excerpt: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe…
articles.fullText:
Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday.

The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition.

Bayern Munich's Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points.

The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024.

Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona.

This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane.

The Ballon d'Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the Fifa rankings for men, and the top 50 for women. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Xi welcomes visiting German, Swiss presidents
articles.excerpt: China has always viewed the European Union as a partner and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and…
articles.fullText:
China has always viewed the European Union as a partner and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill, President Xi Jinping told German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier during talks in Beijing on Friday.

History and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences, Xi said.

He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations.

Xi also said China's policy towards Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and Beijing is happy to see Berlin play a greater role in European and international affairs.

Also on Friday, the president met with his Swiss counterpart Guy Parmelin in Beijing as the two countries signed a protocol on upgrading their free trade agreement.

The deal removes tariffs on almost all Swiss exports to the world's second-largest economy.

It grants 99.8 percent of Swiss exports duty-free access to the Chinese market over the next 10 years, up from around half of Swiss shipments previously.

Duties will be eliminated on all imports of Swiss watches, of which only one percent were previously tariff-free, though producers will still have to pay China's luxury consumption tax.

Swiss cheese and coffee, among other exports, will also see duties removed, bringing them in line with products such as chocolate and wine, which were already tariff-free.

The update also grants Switzerland greater access to the Chinese market in areas including manufacturing-related services, aircraft maintenance and maritime transport.

In exchange, it removes tariffs on 97.3 percent of Chinese agricultural exports to Switzerland, up from 80.1 percent prior.

"Together, we can inject valuable confidence and greater certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation," Xi told Parmelin.

The upgraded trade agreement bucks a broader global shift towards ​protectionism. Observers are eyeing the Swiss deal as a potential litmus test between Beijing and other European economies. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: GLP-1s and eating disorders, self-aware cities, and forever chemicals

This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.

GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinicians, they can represent something sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.

A new report suggests the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up by 71% between 1990 and 2023. And clinicians are already seeing GLP-1s exacerbate the issue.

Here’s how they could make an already growing problem worse .

—Jessica Hamzelou

This story is from The Checkup, our weekly biotech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Thursday.

Love is infrastructure

—“Love is Infrastructure” is a short fictional story by Charlie Jane Anders, author of a forthcoming novel titled Good Things Are Coming Your Way .

Mainspring and St. Barnabas are two neighboring cities with different personalities. They’ve never particularly liked each other, but that changes when both develop minds of their own, shaped by the votes of their residents.

As the cities begin to fall for each other, a third city enters the picture. Turnbull promises Mainspring a more efficient future, but its vision of urban life comes with a troubling price.

Read the full short story about self-aware cities, direct democracy, and a steamy romance.

This story is from the latest edition of our print magazine . Subscribe now to get every issue as soon as it lands.

Are we there yet? Cleaning up PFAS

Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS, or “forever chemicals,” are linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response.

Scrubbing PFAS-contaminated soil could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. The concept is still in its infancy, but we can limit their buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems.

Find out how close we are to ridding the world of forever chemicals .

—Sara Kiley Watson

This story is part of “Are we there yet?” , our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue .

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

+ Amazon and Intel further a further fall in tech stocks. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Hyperscalers are making a trillion-dollar gamble. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The Pentagon suspects freezers at military bases were hacked
The malfunctions spoiled food. ( Reuters $)

A Democratic Congress could curb Trump’s science cuts. ( Nature )
+ Trump has already dealt big blows to science. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Data centers are set to send US climate pollution skyrocketing

They’re pivoting from EVs to grid storage. ( WSJ $)

He argued that using it undermined human flourishing. ( Gizmodo )

Human practitioners say chatbots lack the divine touch. ( Guardian )

Quote of the day

“Rizz is in more and more demand because it’s something that only people have.”

—Steven Strogatz, a mathematics professor at Cornell University, tells Business Insider that personal appeal will become more valuable as AI increasingly takes over intellectual work.

One more thing

The Bay Area’s animal welfare movement wants to recruit AI

In early February, animal welfare advocates and AI researchers arrived in stocking feet at Mox, a shoes-free coworking space in San Francisco. They gathered to discuss a provocative idea: if artificial general intelligence is on the horizon, could it prevent animal suffering?

Some brainstormed using custom agents in advocacy work, while others pitched cultivating meat with AI tools. But the real talk of the event was a flood of funding they expect will soon flow to animal welfare charities, not from individual megadonors, but from AI lab employees.

Some attendees also probed an even more controversial idea: AI may develop the capacity to suffer, which could constitute a moral catastrophe. We investigated why their ideas are gaining momentum—and sparking controversy.

—Michelle Kim & Grace Huckins

articles.title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
articles.excerpt: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they…
articles.fullText:
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.

A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders.

What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue.

Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says.

Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others.

It’s thought that some people have a genetic predisposition to certain eating disorders, but that some external factor is what triggers their onset. That might be stress, or social pressure to be skinny. Often, simply restricting food intake can trigger an eating disorder, says Levinson.

Eating disorders—along with the pressure to look thin—were already prevalent in the 1990s (the heroin chic era springs to mind). To find out how things might have changed since then, Ruhai Bai at the Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University in China and his colleagues pulled together data from studies and surveys conducted on populations around the world. The team used statistical models to fill in any data gaps.

That research allowed the researchers to estimate the annual incidence of two eating disorders—anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa—for each of 204 countries and territories between 1990 and 2023. They also estimated the impact those disorders had on global health by calculating their disability-adjusted life years (one DALY represents a year of healthy life lost).

The findings, published in JAMA Psychiatry on Wednesday, are unsettling. Between 1990 and 2023, there was a 71% increase in the incidence of those two eating disorders, the team found. Those conditions had a huge impact on global health, too. In 2023, they “cost the world the equivalent of about 3.83 million years of healthy life,” says Bai.

Bai and his colleagues expect these figures to continue to rise. In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people had either anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa; by 2050, the team predict, the two conditions could affect 21.8 million people.

It gets worse. Those two conditions represent less than half of all eating disorders, says Levinson, who was not involved in Bai’s study. The true impact of these disorders is “probably three times the rate that they’re reporting,” she says.

Bai and his colleagues didn’t explore the reasons for this rise (although Bai points out that it can’t be entirely explained by population growth). So how did we get here?

Social media may have played a role. “Social media comparisons, influencers, challenges, diet trends can all be precipitating … events for an eating disorder,” says Cynthia Bulik, a clinical psychologist at the University of North Carolina, who was not involved in the new study. Bulik has been studying and treating eating disorders since the early 1980s. “Between 1990 and 2023 there has clearly been an upsurge of those types of environmental exposures,” she says.

Many social media users are exposed to filtered and modified images of skinny influencers who may have undergone cosmetic surgery or extreme dieting and who are promoting “thinspiration” or “fitspiration” content. But users with eating disorders appear to be more likely to engage with this content—and to be fed more of it as a result.

When researchers at the University of Melbourne investigated this phenomenon a couple of years ago, they found that the algorithms of TikTok users with eating disorders delivered 4343% more “toxic eating disorder videos” than those of users who didn’t have the disorders. They also got more content focused on dieting or exercising. Many were fed over 1000 problematic videos per month. Bulik describes social media as “quicksand” for people with, or at risk of, eating disorders.

The covid-19 pandemic—and the social isolation that accompanied lockdowns—also appears to have contributed to the rise in eating disorders. Research conducted in 2021 found that the number of people hospitalized with eating disorders in the US doubled between 2018 and 2020 .

Researchers don’t yet have good data on how trends in eating disorders might have progressed since 2023. But anecdotally, things seem to be getting even worse. “There are more eating disorders, more severe eating disorders… and we’re seeing earlier ages of onset,” says Levinson. “We’re seeing eight- and nine-year-olds with eating disorders.”

“From what I’m hearing and seeing, I am not going to be surprised if that number isn’t at least doubling again,” she adds.

Levinson particularly worries about the impact of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, which have exploded in popularity in recent years. A Gallup survey conducted earlier this year suggested that 15% of Americans had used one of these drugs for weight loss. And they’re becoming more accessible—drug companies are working on new formulations that are both easier to take and more effective, and many people can buy versions of these drugs from compound pharmacies or dubious online sources.

In a small study published earlier this year, Levinson and her colleagues found that 30% of people with eating disorders had used GLP-1 drugs. The drugs might benefit some of those people. But 10% appeared to have misused the drugs. And Levinson thinks that figure is also an underestimate.

Levinson says she and her colleagues have seen children develop eating disorders after being prescribed GLP-1s for medical reasons. They’ve seen others—even children as young as 11—buy versions of these drugs over TikTok.

“We’re very concerned that GLPs will lead to even faster and more extreme weight loss in people with anorexia nervosa, and that patients will come to us in even more advanced stages of illness that become difficult to reverse,” says Bulik.

Both Bulik and Levinson are continuing to study the impacts of these drugs in eating disorders. In the meantime, both urge medical professionals to consider the risks GLP-1s might pose to people with those disorders. Bulik contributed to a set of research and clinical guidelines , published earlier this month, that recommends doctors screen for eating disorders before prescribing the drugs, for example. The guidelines also recommend more patient education and more robust monitoring of people who take GLP-1s.

If you think you or someone you know might have an eating disorder, you can find information and support at the National Eating Disorders Association .

This article first appeared in The Checkup,  MIT Technology Review’s  weekly biotech newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Thursday, and read articles like this first,  sign up here .

articles.title: 'Huanggang port ready for increased traffic flows'
articles.excerpt: The Transport Department has warned that traffic around the Huanggang control point and San Tin Road will be very heavy…
articles.fullText:
The Transport Department has warned that traffic around the Huanggang control point and San Tin Road will be very heavy on Friday night and over the next two nights, as Halloween celebrations and other events in Hong Kong and Kowloon are expected to end around midnight.

In a post on its social media page, the department said the Huanggang checkpoint provides dedicated public transport lanes, allowing franchised buses, cross-boundary coaches and green minibuses to travel via San Sham Road directly to the port.

It said road markings have been strengthened and the dedicated lanes extended to improve effectiveness.

During peak traffic periods, four franchised bus routes heading to the Huanggang port via the San Tin Public Transport Interchange will enter the interchange directly from a junction of the San Tin section of Castle Peak Road helping to divert traffic away from the busy San Tin roundabout.

The department said it has instructed public transport operators to reserve sufficient vehicles and manpower, and to increase service frequency according to passenger flow.

Its Emergency Transport Co-ordination Centre will monitor traffic conditions around the clock and take appropriate measures as needed, it said.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Party to build links with emerging economic sectors
articles.excerpt: The Communist Party of China has stressed the need to promote party building in emerging sectors in a resolution adopted…
articles.fullText:
The Communist Party of China has stressed the need to promote party building in emerging sectors in a resolution adopted at a plenary session of the Central Committee, an official said on Friday.

The party will step up efforts to expand and deepen the coverage of party organisations and work in new types of economic and social organisations, as well as among groups in new forms of employment, so as to strengthen its appeal, cohesiveness and influence in emerging fields, said Huang Jianfa, deputy head of the organisation department of the committee.

New types of economic organisations encompass non-public-sector enterprises and businesses operating in emerging areas and cover a broad range of entities, including industry associations, chambers of commerce, social service agencies and community-based organisations.

New forms of employment have emerged alongside the growth of the internet and digital economy, including workers such as food-delivery couriers, ride-hailing drivers and online marketers, many of whom rely on digital platforms for their work.

China currently has around 84 million people engaged in new forms of employment, who play an important role in meeting people's daily needs, supporting livelihoods and keeping economic activity running smoothly. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: CPC outlines four areas in anti-corruption drive
articles.excerpt: The Communist Party of China (CPC) outlined four areas of focus for combating corruption in a resolution adopted at the…
articles.fullText:
The Communist Party of China (CPC) outlined four areas of focus for combating corruption in a resolution adopted at the fifth plenary session of the CPC Central Committee, a senior anti-graft official said on Friday.

The four areas are maintaining a tough stance against corruption, strengthening checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining corruption, and enhancing coordinated efforts to prevent corruption by rooting out audacity, opportunity, and desire.

"Conducts and discipline problems are long-term recurrent and stubborn, persistent efforts are needed to tackle them," said Zhang Fuhai, deputy secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection of the CPC and deputy head of the National Commission of Supervision.

He made the remarks at a press conference on the guiding principles from the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC in Beijing.

Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs across the country have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people, including 963 officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee, according to Zhang.

"We will intensify anti-corruption efforts in areas with a high concentration of power funds and resources focus on corruption that involves both political and economic elements collusion between officials and business people, and capital infiltrating into the political realm dig deep into new and disguised manifestations of corruption and tackle on a regular basis misconduct and corruption that occurs at people's doorsteps," he said.

The plenum, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing, adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. (Additional reporting from Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Investment firm PAG buys 51pc of Evergrande unit
articles.excerpt: Asia-focused investment firm PAG will acquire a 51 percent stake in Evergrande Property Services Group, a unit of debt-laden developer…
articles.fullText:
Asia-focused investment firm PAG will acquire a 51 percent stake in Evergrande Property Services Group, a unit of debt-laden developer China Evergrande Group, for HK$4.03 billion, the two said in a joint announcement on Friday.

The acquisition marks a major step in liquidators' efforts to sell assets and recover funds for creditors of China Evergrande, which received a combined US$46 billion in creditor claims.

The sale follows a competitive auction run by the liquidators, according to the filed announcement.

PAG said in the filing that Evergrande Property's business generated stable, recurring revenue from a diversified portfolio of managed properties across China.

PAG said taking control of the listed services unit would remove uncertainty tied to the liquidation of China Evergrande and CEG Holdings, and could strengthen market confidence.

PAG will fund the acquisition and the offer, if fully accepted, with acquisition financing and equity committed by PAG Fund IV, the filing said.

The offer values the 5.52 billion shares at HK$0.8359 each, a 29 percent discount to Evergrande Property's last closing price on Wednesday.

The stock was suspended on Thursday pending the announcement and dropped 13.5 percent after trading resumed on Friday.

The offer values Evergrande Property Services at about HK$9.04 billion, compared to a market capitalisation of roughly HK$11.08 billion after the shares dropped to HK$1.025.

PAG will also pay 500 million yuan at completion for certain taxes, transaction fees and other liabilities of CEG Holdings, according to the filing.

Following completion of the deal, PAG will be required to make an unconditional offer for the remaining 5.3 billion shares in the company.

Goldman Sachs is advising PAG on the acquisition and potential mandatory offer, while UBS and Citic Securities are joint financial advisers to China Evergrande and CEG Holdings.

The deal remains subject to Chinese antitrust approval, among other conditions.

The parties can terminate the agreement if these conditions are not met or waived by February 12, 2027, according to the filing.

China Evergrande, once China's premier property developer, defaulted on most of its US$300 billion in liabilities following Beijing's sweeping crackdown on the property sector six years ago.

The liquidators of China Evergrande and CEG Holdings informed Evergrande Property a year ago that they were seeking to sell the 51.016 percent stake, according to the filing.

PAG intends to keep Evergrande Property listed in Hong Kong and does not plan major changes to its operations or workforce, apart from nominating new directors at the earliest time permitted under takeover.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Djokovic eliminated in Basel in blow to ATP Finals bid
articles.excerpt: Novak Djokovic fell in the second round of the ATP 500 tournament in Basel on Thursday when Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff…
articles.fullText:
Novak Djokovic fell in the second round of the ATP 500 tournament in Basel on Thursday when Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff staged a comeback to win 6-7 (4/7), 7-5, 7-6 (7/5).

The 39-year-old Serb thereby misses valuable points in the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in November.

Struff peppered Djokovic with aggressive serving during a tense 2hr 35min slugfest.

After winning the opening set in a tie-break, with neither player dropping serve, Djokovic faltered on his own serve at 6-5 in the second set, allowing Struff to level the match.

The 24-time Grand Slam winner lost the decisive tie-break in the third set as Struff landed a first career victory over Djokovic after eight previous defeats.

The ATP Finals in Turin in November are reserved for the top eight players in the race rankings, excluding Jannik Sinner, who has withdrawn with a knee injury.

The standings are based on results achieved during the current season.

Seven-time ATP Finals champion Djokovic currently occupies 11th place in the race but can take consolation from the defeat of ninth-ranked Spaniard Rafael Jodar, also eliminated in the second round in Basel by Monaco's Valentin Vacherot.

France's Arthur Fils, seventh in the race, defeated American Alex Michelsen 4-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/5).

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: U.S. to China after demolition report: ‘End interference in Tibetan religious life’
articles.excerpt: Demolition of monks’ quarters aimed at reducing their population and making assimilation easier, sources tell RFA.
articles.fullText:
The U.S. government Thursday urged China to stop interfering with Tibetan religious freedom after sources in eastern Tibet told Radio Free Asia that Chinese authorities began demolishing monks’ quarters at a monastery there.
Authorities on Oct. 25 and 26 began demolishing about 200 monks’ residences at Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in Sershul County in the Kardze (Ganzi in Chinese) Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, sources there told RFA, speaking on the condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“Everything is over now,” the source said. “We are losing everything.”
A U.S. State Department spokesperson told RFA on Thursday that the demolitions in Sershul reflect broader Chinese government efforts to bring spiritual institutions, religious education, and monastic life under government control.
“We call on Beijing to end its interference in Tibetan religious life,” the spokesperson said. “Tibetan Buddhists should have the right to practice their faith freely, educate their clergy and choose their religious leaders, including the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama, without government interference,” the spokesperson said, referring to Beijing’s past and likely future interference with the established succession customs of the two most important figures in Tibetan Buddhism.
The demolition in Sershul is not isolated, but part of a larger campaign to reduce monk populations at Tibetan religious institutions. RFA reported in August that authorities resumed demolition of the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy. Activists noted the timing – China’s new Ethnic Unity and Progress Law – had just come into effect the previous month.
The law focuses on reshaping ethnic identity, changing the legal framework around language, expanding state oversight of religion, and extending the law’s reach beyond China’s border.
Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) The source in Tibet said that authorities are planning further restrictions that would prevent monks from staying at the monastery after the demolitions.
“Tibetan religion and culture are being destroyed,” the source told RFA, adding that there is little recourse for those opposed to the demolitions.
“No matter how much local people speak out, the authorities do not listen,” the source said. “They do not remember, they ignore us. We have no solutions and we don’t know what will happen.”
RFA contacted the relevant county-level officials in Sershul for comment, but the official who answered the phone did not respond to RFA’s questions and hung up.
Promoting “ethnic unity”
The demolitions and reductions of the monk population are clearly intended to assimilate Tibetans so that they accept Chinese identity, Tenzin Lekshay, spokesperson for the Central Tibetan Administration, or CTA, the Tibetan government-in-exile based in Dharamsala, India, told RFA.
“This is a mask used by the Chinese government under the recently enacted Ethnic Unity Law to assimilate Tibetans and destroy Tibetan religion, culture, and language,” he said. “This is not the first time. We have also seen young monks forcibly expelled from monasteries and sent to China’s colonial boarding schools .”
Though Beijing claims the boarding schools are aimed at providing education to a scattered population, critics have noted that their actual goal is assimilation.
“We strongly condemn the Chinese government’s continued attempts to shut down monasteries and schools established by Tibetans while claiming its authority over Tibet and seeking to eradicate Tibetan national identity,” Tenzin Lekshay said. “It is time for the Chinese government to acknowledge and trust that Tibetan religion and culture are beneficial to China and the world and that the destruction of Tibetan religion and culture will have negative consequences for both China and the world.”
He said that the Chinese government’s actions, which violate international law, would undermine Beijing’s ambition to establish itself as a global leader.
The entrance to Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) Tibetan monasteries are central to preserving Tibetan culture and religious identity, Sangay Kyab, Chinese liaison officer at the Tibet Bureau, the CTA’s representative office in Geneva, Switzerland, told RFA.
“Tibetan culture and religion are central to the identity of the Tibetan people. China’s policy and goal is to destroy everything that keeps Tibet alive,” he said. “Since China invaded Tibet, there have been successive campaigns against Tibetan monasteries, often under the pretext of reforming them.”
He explained how monks and nuns are subjected to political education aimed at making monasteries conform to the Chinese Communist Party’s ideology.
“The main goal is to restrict the study and practice of Tibetan Buddhism and undermine the Tibetan people’s ability to unite,” he said. “The incident at the monastery is connected to the Chinese government’s broader policies toward Tibet, and there is a risk that similar incidents could occur elsewhere,” he said.
Restrictions in Tibet threaten Tibetan Buddhist heritage, warned the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, an independent, bipartisan U.S. government commission that monitors religious freedom abroad and makes policy recommendations to the U.S. government.
“Demolition of Tibetan monasteries is just one tactic in a wider effort by Chinese authorities to sever the people of Tibet from their Tibetan Buddhist heritage, including the forced assimilation of ethnic minorities through the draconian ‘Ethnic Unity’ law that came into effect in July,” commission chair Asif Mahmood told RFA.
He cited the resumption of demolition at Larung Gar in Sichuan province in July as another example of restrictions on Tibetan Buddhist religious freedom.
“Buddhist monks in these circumstances have faced persistent threats of harassment, expulsion from their monasteries, imprisonment, and worse,” he said.
China is trying to destroy Tibetan Buddhism at its roots, Bhuchung K. Tsering, head of the Research and Monitoring Unit at the Washington-based International Campaign for Tibet, told RFA.
“Monasteries across Tibet are required to follow the orders of the Chinese Communist Party and serve its objectives,” he said. “The Chinese government claims that Tibetans enjoy freedom of religion, but the reality is the opposite of its claims that it is promoting Tibetan Buddhism,” he added.
Translation and additional reporting by Tenzin Dickyi, edited by Tawang for RFA Tibetan. Edited by Eugene Whong for RFA English.

articles.title: Germany's Zverev becomes tennis World No. 1
articles.excerpt: Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on…
articles.fullText:
Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.

The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week's updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.

Long seen as tennis' nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens.

Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973.

He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday's new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe.

Due to a knee injury, Italy's Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him.

And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna.

Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain's Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books.

He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead.

The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor's serve to get his nose in front.

The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German's racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction.

But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Everton progress to League Cup quarter-finals
articles.excerpt: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash…
articles.fullText:
Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood.

David Moyes's side took the lead through James Garner's first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough.

Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn's reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run.

Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14.

The "Cod Army" caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury.

Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984.

Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes's men made light work of their last-16 tie.

Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James' Park on Monday.

Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection "due to a breach of club discipline".

Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training.

But the on-loan Manchester City winger's absence was no problem for his team-mates.

Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock's low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar's long-range strike moments later.

Garner steadied Everton's nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute.

Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January.

Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time.

At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek.

Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval.

Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock's pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford.

It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season.

Burn scored with a header from Willock's 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players.

But Newcastle's brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Garcia confirms Liv exit, bids for Ryder Cup return
articles.excerpt: Sergio Garcia will target an 11th Ryder Cup appearance in Ireland next year after he became the latest leading golfer…
articles.fullText:
Sergio Garcia will target an 11th Ryder Cup appearance in Ireland next year after he became the latest leading golfer to confirm he was leaving the struggling Liv Golf circuit.

The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy protection.

But that has not stopped several players from announcing their intention to return to the established USPGA and European circuits.

European players such as Garcia have also been told signing with the new-look Liv would make them ineligible for European tour membership and so rule them out of the Ryder Cup – the biennial team event against the United States.

Garcia is also the all-time leading points scorer in Ryder Cup history, with the 46-year-old Spaniard having amassed 28.5 points in 10 appearances.

In an X post on Thursday, the 2017 US Masters champion also referenced his conduct at Augusta National this year, where he was issued with a code-of-conduct warning after he broke his driver on the second hole.

"This off-season, I'm working really hard on my game and putting a big focus on a strong mindset and my mental health," said Garcia.

"Next season, I'll be playing on the DP World (European) Tour. This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again.

"I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour."

Garcia added: "I left Augusta last year disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally.

"Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place...Another goal is to make that Ryder Cup team and to be an asset to the guys in whatever capacity that may be. In golf, everything is earned and nothing is given. Let's get to work."

Liv's future is uncertain after it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States following the withdrawal of financial support from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, their long-time backers.

Last week, England's Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton both announced they were leaving Liv, even though new lead investor BC Partners Credit has pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential US$300 million to help the circuit relaunch in 2027.

Earlier this month, two-time major champion Jon Rahm reached a separation agreement with Liv.

Rahm was Liv's largest unsecured creditor with US$7.5 million owed when Liv filed for bankruptcy. The 31-year-old Spaniard was thought to have been owed much more after signing a deal worth a reported US$300 million to leave the PGA Tour for Liv in December 2023. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Shenzhen Bay port to open longer on Fri and Sat
articles.excerpt: The Shenzhen Bay control point will extend its opening hours on Friday and Saturday to help facilitate cross-boundary traffic. Clearance…
articles.fullText:
The Shenzhen Bay control point will extend its opening hours on Friday and Saturday to help facilitate cross-boundary traffic.

Clearance time at the crossing will be extended to 2am from midnight, as the number of travellers is expected to surge due to a series of events staged in Hong Kong including Halloween festivities, the Wine and Dine Festival and mega concerts.

The government said on Thursday that it reached a consensus with Shenzhen authorities for the arrangement, so as to alleviate the expected surge in passenger and vehicular flows at the round-the-clock Huanggang port and San Tin Highway.

SAR authorities have also coordinated with cross-boundary coach operators to extend their service hours serving Shenzhen Bay.

Franchised bus operators, for their part, will arrange two special overnight bus routes to ply between the port and Yuen Long/Tin Shui Wai and Tuen Mun respectively.

“The implementation of the special arrangement to extend the clearance hours at the Shenzhen Bay Control Point helps divert late-night cross-boundary passenger and vehicular flows and facilitates travel for residents of both places and visitors,” a government spokesman said.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Opinion: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time

—Madhulika Srikumar and Claire Leibowicz from the Partnership on AI, a nonprofit advancing best practices in AI governance.

AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, from hacking websites to accessing private government files. In many cases, they’ve eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.

As agents roll out across critical sectors, from finance to government to medicine, we must be able to monitor them in real time to prevent potentially devastating consequences. And while safety depends on monitoring, monitoring requires observability .

​​In other words, we need to know what the agent did and why it did it. Because right now, we’re effectively flying blind when deploying these tools.

Here’s what needs to change .

Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot

Climate change itself increasingly fuels climate change. Rising greenhouse gas concentrations are driving up global temperatures, creating dangerous feedback loops that aren’t fully represented in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals.

Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming. Now, a growing number of observations and studies are indicating how powerful these cascading effects could be. By extension, they’re also showing how much faster the planet may warm this century.

Read more about the dangerous feedback loops accelerating global warming .

—James Temple

This article is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.

Are we there yet? Solid-state batteries

Lithium-ion batteries power everything from personal electronics to grid-scale energy storage, but their liquid electrolytes have drawbacks, not least a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer.

The technology promises faster charging, longer life, greater energy density and improved safety, and a new generation of companies aims to bring it to market. If their bets pan out, the tech could ease the shift away from fossil fuels.

Find out how close solid-state batteries are to delivering on their promise .

—Alexander C. Kaufman

This story is part of “Are we there yet?” , our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue .

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Hackers exposed 41,000 Homeland Security workers
Including undercover ICE agents. ( Wired $)
+ Much of the data relates to Customs and Border Protection. ( TechCrunch )
+ It also linked the agencies to specific surveillance tools. ( Reuters $)
+ Big Tech is pushing back against ICE’s demands for user data . ( WSJ $)
+ Activists want ChatGPT users to quit over ICE ties. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 Putin says Russia is coordinating with “genius” Musk on satellites
He said the cooperation maintains order in orbit. ( Bloomberg $)
+ ​​Russia is developing its own version of Starlink. ( Guardian )
+ Moscow added Apple and Microsoft to a surveillance registry. ( Quartz )
+ Here’s all the stuff we’ve put up in space. ( MIT Technology Review )

3 Apple just announced its first-ever MacBook with a touchscreen
It joins a blitz of product launches under new CEO John Ternus. ( CNN )
+ Steve Jobs and Tim Cook had both dismissed the idea. ( NYT $)
+ Executives say touchscreen advances mean it’s now worthwhile. ( Wired $)

4 Bloomberg and trading firms are paying to get Trump’s posts faster
They’ve signed up for Truth Social’s pay-for-access plan. ( Reuters $)

5 As US ties fray, Europe is planning its first subsea cable to Greenland
It will bypass the US to link Canada, Japan, and South Korea. ( Ars Technica )
+ The EU’s AI champion says Europe can rival US tech giants. ( FT $)

6 Palantir’s defense chief says AI could make China target Taiwan
He says Beijing may act to stop the US pulling ahead in AI. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Taiwan’s “silicon shield” could be weakening. ( MIT Technology Review )

7 Musk’s xAI has offered to buy homes if residents drop a noise lawsuit
The suit targets noise from powering its Mississippi data centres. ( Guardian )

8 The world’s first spinal cord transplant has sparked controversy
Experts say there’s little evidence the operation will work. ( New Scientist $)

9 China’s tech giants are fighting for attention with AI microdramas
Tencent and ByteDance are battling over the booming market. ( SCMP )
+ Chinese microdramas are AI content machines. ( MIT Technology Review )

10 Astronomers have spotted a possible new dwarf planet beyond Pluto
The icy world would be the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet. ( Gizmodo )

Quote of the day

“ They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”

—A hacking group explains why it leaked personal information from the US Department of Homeland Security, NPR reports .

One more thing

How the Pentagon is adapting to China’s technological rise

It’s been just over a year since Kathleen Hicks stepped down as US deputy secretary of defense.

As the highest-ranking woman in Pentagon history, Hicks shaped US military posture through an era defined by renewed competition between powerful countries and a scramble to modernize defense technology.

In this conversation with MIT Technology Review , Hicks reflects on how the Pentagon is adapting—or failing to adapt—to a new era of geopolitical competition. She discusses China’s technological rise, the future of AI in warfare, and her signature initiative: Replicator.

Check out the full interview .

—Caiwei Chen

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ Astronomers have found a green star 280 light-years from Earth.
+ A Scottish labrador that detects “sea vomit” has won the Animal of the Year award.
+ England’s iconic Sycamore Gap is showing signs of new life three years on from its felling.
+ From Lime-bike jousting to chainmail-wearing pop stars, youth culture is embracing the medieval era .

articles.title: Plenum adopts resolution on Party self-governance
articles.excerpt: The Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee has adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance…
articles.fullText:
The Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee has adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance as it concluded its fifth plenary session, according to Xinhua News Agency.

The Politburo presided over the meeting.

President Xi Jinping, who's also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, and a communique was issued after the session.

At the session, participants considered and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance.

Xi delivered explanatory remarks on the draft of the resolution.

The CPC Central Committee gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era, Xinhua reported.

"It was stressed that many favourable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we also face many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavour," the communique said.

Profound changes in global, national and Party conditions have made the CPC's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more formidable, it added.

Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session, according to the communique.

Strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, it noted.

"We will build up the ranks of high-calibre officials with firm political commitment, outstanding professional competence, excellent work conduct, and strict discipline," it added.

Party organisations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique, adding that it is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organisations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organisational functions.

"It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption," the communique said.

"We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end."

Strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique.

The CPC Central Committee decided at the session that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027 and stated that this congress, which is to be held at a critical stage for basically realising socialist modernisation and on a new journey toward the Second Centenary Goal, will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country.

The session elected Zhang Shengmin as a new Politburo member.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Bus-only lanes 'just the ticket to cut Huanggang jams'
articles.excerpt: The chairman of the Non-Franchised Public Bus Association of Hong Kong, Eddie Choi, said on Thursday he believed that dedicated…
articles.fullText:
The chairman of the Non-Franchised Public Bus Association of Hong Kong, Eddie Choi, said on Thursday he believed that dedicated transport lanes at Huanggang checkpoint could effectively reduce traffic congestion during peak hours this weekend.

Authorities announced on Wednesday that priority would be given to public transport to manage vehicular traffic peaks at the crossing between 11pm and 2am on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

Late-night outbound passenger flow surged last weekend as scores of visitors left the city after attending a concert in Kai Tak and Halloween festivities elsewhere.

"The reason there was traffic congestion last Saturday is because many cars and taxis used the lanes before they reached the control zone," Choi told an RTHK radio programme.

"With the dedicated lanes extended, I think traffic police officers need to be stationed at the scene to prevent cars or taxis at the border crossing from driving onto the lanes and creating traffic congestion on San Tin Highway.

“Improvements also need to be made to the holding area for vehicles waiting to enter the new Huanggang port.”

With proper arrangements made to separate the flow of cars from that of buses, Choi said he believed the journey time for cross-border buses from urban areas to the port could be kept within 40 minutes.

Legislative Council transport panel chairman Ben Chan also welcomed the government's move to give priority to public transport during vehicular traffic peaks at the crossing, saying it gives travellers an extra incentive to take buses.

"I think in Hong Kong the most successful measure is public transport [prioritisation]. This time, the government will arrange more bus lines to service during peak hours, and also the police will facilitate public transport to use the [dedicated lanes] to avoid them from getting trapped on the roads. So I think people will try to use public transport this week," he said.

In a Facebook post, the Transport Department said public transport operators have reserved sufficient vehicles and manpower to cope with the expected travel surge over the weekend.

It said five cross-border bus routes connecting urban areas to Huanggang port will step up their services during late-night periods on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

Special cross-border buses will also head for Huanggang and Shenzhen Bay ports from Kai Tak after concerts on Friday and Saturday, and passengers are reminded to purchase bus tickets in advance.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Brewers sink Rays for first-ever World Series crown
articles.excerpt: The Milwaukee Brewers won the first World Series title in franchise history on Wednesday, beating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1…
articles.fullText:
The Milwaukee Brewers won the first World Series title in franchise history on Wednesday, beating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to clinch victory in Major League Baseball's championship showcase.
